Subject:- Forwarding of important judgement by Hon'ble High Court
in WP No, 4948/2011, APFC, R.O Nagpur Vs. M/s Sai
Constructions Company-regarding,

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith a copy of the judgement delivered
by Hon'ble High Court, Bombay, Nagpur Bench in WP No, 4946/2011, dated
21.01.2013 (copy enciosed).

2. in the instant matter, while dismissing the above petition,
Hon'ble Court has relied upon the division bench judgement in LPA No, 320
of 2012 filed in WP No. 5147 of 2011 (Taj Tibbiya College and Rasheeda
Hospital, Nalsaheb Road, Nagpur Vs, RPFC, Nagpur). The gist of the said
order Is reproduced below:

"The instant appeal is challenged basically on the ground that the
APFC is a quasi-judidal authority and as such, the petition at his
behest was not tenable.

Though the APFC also performs the duties of the quasi-judicial
authority, at the same time, he is enjoined upon certain enforcement
duties under the provident fund Act, in order to protect the interest of
the employees.

In that view of the matter, we do not see any reason to interfere
in the impugned order challenged in the instant appeal”.

Lf2

3. In the light of above observation, the Hon'ble Court held that
section 5-D of the EPF Act confers a power upon the Assistant Provident
Fund Commissioner to efficiently administer the scheme framed under the
said Act and he has got the duty to see that the interest of the employees
are protected. In view of this, the objection regarding maintainability of the
Writ Petition on the ground that APFC being a quasi-judicial authority cannot
file Writ, is rejected.

4. Therefore, this landmark order of Hon’ble court, Bombay, Nagpur
Bench may be kept in mind while defending the similar cases.
Yours faithfully,

Subject: Online e-Return Format for PF Exempted/Relaxed Establishments.
Sir,

As part of e-governance programme of EPFO, an online e-Return format for the
establishments having relaxation or exemption from the provisions of the EPF Scheme, 1952,
under Section 17(1)(a) and 17(2) (read with Paragraph 27A of the EPF Scheme, 1952) of the EPF
&% MP Act, 1952 was launched by Hon ble Chairman, CBT, EPF and Union Labour & Employment
Minister on 12.01.2014. Establishments who have been granted exemption by an order of the
RPEC for individual employee(s) under the provisions contained in Paragraph 27 of the EPF
Scheme, 1952 are also required to file the e-return periodically.

2. Thus any establishment whether exempted by way of notification by the
Appropriate Government or relaxed by an order of the RPFC Is required to file the e-Return.
This is a mandatory return from 01.04.2014 onwards or from the date of grant of
exemption/relaxation, whichever !s later. All such existing establishments have to compulsorily

file the e-return as on 31.03.2014 (for the year 2013-14) and thereafter at regular monthly
intervals.

3. Following are the salient features of the Return:

I. The e-Return has 6 modules: A, B, C, D, E, and F.
ll. Modules A and B are related to basic details of the establishment and the Trust

respectively. These two modules require one time data-entry: however, later
editing is enabled.

Page lof3

Vi.

Vil.

Vill.

4.

Modules C and D are related to employment and contribution details in respect of
the EEs, respectively. Details in these two modules are required to be filled on a
monthly basis.

Module E provides for giving details of investment. It is also required to be filled ona
monthly basis. However, it is meant for only such exempted or relaxed
establishments which are also maintaining the Trust of their own. If an
exempted/relaxed establishment is not maintaining a Trust of its own and is a
participating unit in a common provident fund Trust maintained by some other
establishment, it is not required to fill this module. However, it will be able to view
the details filled by the common Trust.

Module F provides for filling details regarding audit, annual statement of accounts
and financial health of the Trust. This will be a yearly exercise. This module can be
opened only at the end of the Financial Year.

The link for filing the return will be through the ECR Portal, once the employer has
logged in. The link will appear only against establishments that are relaxed or
exempted. RPFCs of the ROs and SROs will have the rights to add any code number
to the list so that such establishments can also start filing the return.

At present the list of exempted establishments as collected from the field offices
have been provided on the portal. Establishment which figure in the list will be able
to file the return.

On cancellation of exemption or withdrawal of relaxation the RPFCs will have the
right to block the return filing from a particular month. However, viewing and/or
filing of the return of earlier period will be permissible.

The establishments which are complying as exempted/relaxed by virtue of having a
sub-code or separate code for administrative convenience will not be required to file
the return. This is irrespective of the fact that the establishment bearing the subcode or separate code is in the jurisdiction of the same RPFC or under another RPFC
where the main establishment is covered. In each cases, the main establishment will
have to add its branches having separate codes or sub-codes.

Elaborate data-field-wise instructions for the guidance of the employers of

exempted/relaxed establishments as well as the field offices have been prepared and are
annexed herewith.

>;

Output report formats for the users such as the RPFCs of field offices, Zonal Additional

CPFCs, Head Office and the employers of the exempted/relaxed establishments and the Trusts
is under development. Valuable feedback of RPFCs and ACCs as well as of employers and the
Trusts is solicited in order to make it more useful from end-user point of view. Likewise format
for monitoring dashboards may also please be suggested.

6.

Zonal ACCs and Regional PF Commissioners are requested to suggest probable FAQs on

the business side to EPF Headquarters for compilation and issue.

1.
Sub-para 7 of para 36 of the Employees'
Provident Fund Scheme 1952 states as under:-
(7)Every employer shall send to the Commissioner such returns in electronic format also, in such
form and manner as may be specified by the Commissioner.
2.
The Employees
Provident
Fund Organisation
has now embarked
upon its next phase of e-govemance
refonns with a view to make its services available to its stakeholders in an efficient, transparent
and reliable manner
and at low costs. In order to make the same successful it is necessary that establishments
furnish electronically
authenticated records through the use of Digital Signature (Class 2 and above) while submitting
statutory returns,
claim forms and other infonnation
requests etc.
3.
The Infonnation Technology Act, 2000 provides for use of Digital Signatures on the documents submitted
in electronic form in order to ensure their security and authenticity.
Digital Signatures
facilitate
creating legally
enforceable electronic
records and eliminate the need to print documents for signing. Digital Signatures
provide
the following three features:-
i)
AuthenticationDigital signatures are used to authenticate the source of messages. The ownership
of a digital signature key is bound to a specific user and thus a valid signature shows that the message
was sent by that user.
ii)
Integrity
- Digital signatures
provide assurance to the sender and receiver of a message that the
message has not been altered during transmission.
iii)
Non Repudiation
- Digital signatures ensure that the sender who has signed the information cannot
at a later time deny having signed it.
4.
Now, in exercise of powers in accordance
with para 36(7) of the Employees'
Provident
Fund Scheme
1952, it is directed that establishments
covered under the Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous
Provisions
Act 1952 shall mandatorily
register at least one Digital Signature Certificate
(DSC), Class 2 and above of their
employerts)
and/or its authorized
signatory(ies)
with the Employees'
Provident
Fund Organisation
as per the
following schedule:-
i)
Establishments
with more than 500 ECR members - by 30.04.2014.
ii)
Establishments
with 101-500 ECR members - by 30.06.2014
4.
As regards establishments
having less than or equal to 100 ECR members,
separate instructions
shall
be issued later. However, it will be in the interest of such establishments
to also register their DSC as e-govemance
mode will require their DSCs also in near future.

Subject : Contribution under Section 6 not payable on Cost to Company(CTC) —
Clarification - Regarding.

It is observed that the import of Section 6 of the Employees’ Provident Funds &
Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 is not correctly understood by some of the field offices
which results in complaints and is many a times a cause for unnecessary litigation. They are
unwittingly asking employers not only to pay contributions on Cost to Company (CTC) but
are also questioning them on why reflecting of employer’s contribution (to PF) under CT C
be not treated as a deduction by them from employees’ salary and consequently why this

be not treated as a violation by the employer of Paragraph 31 of the Employees’ Provident
Scheme, 1952.

2. Many of the employers in today’s world give the breakup of the outgoings under
different heads as CTC in the appointment letter issued to a new employee. CTC is the total
cost, generally on an yearly basis, which an employer incurs on an employee during his
employment/services or his holding office in the company/establishment and Is

normally/generally much above the wage ceiling on which PF is payable under the Act and
the Schemes.

3. “Basic wages” as defined under section 2(b) of the Act means “all emoluments

which are earned by an employee while on duty or on leave ... In accordance with the terms

of the contract of employment ... but does not include-" among other things —

Page 1 of 3

HRA

Overtime Allowance
Bonus

Commission or

any other similar allowance payable to the employee.

4. Section 6 which deals with ‘Contribution’ says that “The contribution which
shall be paid by the employer to the Fund shall be” a certain percentage ‘of the basic
wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance (if any) for the time being
payable to each of the employees...”. Thus, contribution under section 6 is payable only on
basic wages (which excludes HRA, Overtime Allowance, Bonus, Commission etc. ), dearness
allowance (which includes cash value of any food concession) and retaining allowance, if
any.

5. Emoluments means all earnings by an employee for the work done by him in an
establishment and includes Bonus, Commission etc. whereas, basic wages (as defined in
the Act) expressly excludes these items/components.

6, CTC cannot be therefore construed to mean ‘emoluments’ which are earned by
an employee within the meaning of the term “basic wages” as given under section 2(b) of
the Act and contribution under section 6 of the Act cannot be thus charged on CITC.

Subject: Fixed medical allowance payable to the serving as well as retired
employees of the EPFO for outdoor treatment-Clarification

Reference: HRM-8/V/12(1)2003/FMA/Vol.-II/6160 dated 13.06.2013

Sir/Madam,

The Employees & Pensioners of the EPFO, who are not covered under Central
Government Health Scheme, (CGHS) are paid Fixed Medical Allowance (FMA) per month to
cater to the cost of medicines/treatment etc. where hospitalization is not involved. At
present, FMA is being given to employees/pensioners @ Rs. 2000 p.m.

Several references have been received regarding admissibility of Fixed Medical Allowance to
both the spouse ,who are working or retired. In this regard it is clarified as under:-

a) In the following cases, only one of the spouse will be eligible for the facility of Fixed
Medical Allowance

i) Ifboth husband and wife are working in the EPF Organisation or both of them have
retired from EPFO & are in same station.

ii) In case where one is EPFO employee & the spouse is EPFO pensioner & are in same
station.

iii) In case where one is serving/retired official of EPFO and spouse is serving/retired
Government or any other organization (including private Firm/Office).

Notwithstanding anything said above, if any one of the spouse is posted outside station
(working), residing separately and need medical facilities as per entitlement without
spouse, then both of them will be eligible for FMA.

b) As per the aforementioned circular dated 13.06.2013, if two or more members of ‘family’
are working in the EPFO, only one of them will be eligible for the facility of Fixed
Medical Allowance. In this regard, it is further clarified that besides the spouse, other
members of the ‘family’ as defined in CS (MA) Rules, 1944, who are working in EPFO &
who are not dependent and also not residing with govt. servant shall be considered as a
separate entity.

P.7.o

c) In the case of an EPFO employee whose wife/husband is an employee of a Government
or any other organization (including private Firm/Office) he/she will be required to give
an undertaking that his/her spouse is not availing of medical facilities in cash, if any,
granted by their respective employers, so as to be eligible to receive FMA in EPFO.

Last Inspection

e Record the date of last visit.

(satisfactory/unsatisfactory)

ACCOUNTS

e Check whether daily entry of claims received through dak is being done

reconciliation.

and not current accounts.

e Record areas where there is no responses on the part of the bank on the issues
raised by the RO/SRO.

Sub: Online availability
of Annexure-K
in respect of Exempted establishments.
Sir,
A large number of grievances are received from the exempted
establishments
on account
of non-receipt
or late receipt of Annexure-K
in respect of their employees who are EPF members
and have preferred
claims for transfer
of their
P.F. accumulations
on shifting
of their jobs from
unexempted
establishment
to exempted establishment.
2.
On
analysis
of
the
grievance
cases,
it
has
been
noticed
that
although
the
P.F.
accumulations
are transferred
in time from concerned field offices to the exempted Trust through
NEFT, the exempted
Trust are unable to credit the same to the members'
account due to nonreceipt or late receipt of corresponding
Annexure-K from the field offices.
3.
To address the issue, a functionality
has been developed
whereby
the field
offices
can
generate
and upload
the
PDF file
of Annexure-K
in respect
of such members
where
the
P.F.
accumulations
are transferred
from
P.F. account
maintained
with
field office to Trust. The user
manual for the following
activities is placed at the Annexure-I:
(a) Generation
of tarz file in the application
software &
(b) Uploading the same on RO/SRO Admin Portal.
4.
The
PDF file
of
Annexure-K,
so
uploaded,
would
be
available
to
the
exempted
establishment
in their
log-in under Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP). An option to search the
Annexure-K
within
specified
time
period
(From
"date"
to
"date")
on the
basis of "Previous
Member
Id", "Present
Member
Id" or "Amount"
has also been provided. The screenshots for the
process at the end of exempted
establishments
are placed at Annexure-II.
It may be noted that
(a) The log-in credentials will be same as that of ECRportal for establishments.
(b) Annexure-K PDFswould be available for download
only to the exempted
establishment
in
their logins.

5.
Further, the PDF files of uploaded
Annexure-K
are also made available to the transfer-inoffices,
which
maintain
the
Pension
Account
of
such
members.
The transfer-in-offices
can
download
the PDF Files from their log-in in RO/SRO Admin Portal. The screenshots for the process
are placed at Annexure-III.
6.
The availability
of Annexure-K
on the
portal
would
mitigate
many
of the
avoidable
grievances in advance. It is expected that all the field office would
(i) generate
the
above
mentioned
files
on the
server
and
upload
them
on
the
portal
immediately
at the first instance and on weekly basis thereafter
as explained
in Annexure-I,
(ii) download
Annexure-K
PDF files uploaded
by other offices as explained
in Annexure-III
and
(iii) familiarize
the exempted
establishments/
Trusts on the new feature
provided
to them to
download
Annexure-K
PDFfiles using their OTCP logins as explained
in Annexure-II.

Subject:- Declaration of result of Examination for promotion to the post of Enforcement
Officer / Accounts Officer held from 08" to 12" October,2012 -Marks of
candidates

Sir / Madam,

The result of the Departmental Examination for promotion to the post of
Enforcement Officer / Accounts Officer held from 08" to 12 October, 2012 has been
declared vide letter No. Exam.5(1)2011/706 dated 28.01.2014(Circular No. 698 of website)
on the above subject.

The paper wise marks of all candidates who had appeared in ali 5 papers is
enclosed herewith for information of all candidates.

It is once again reiterated that the said result has been prepared based on the
Provisions of the Enforcement Officer / Assistant Accounts Officer and Superintendent
Departmental Competitive Examination Scheme, 2002 as amended from time to time. The
number of candidates declared successful in respect of each Region/State (erstwhile Region)
are only to the extent of vacancies notified for that Region / State (erstwhile Region). Even
if a General Category candidate obtains at least 40% marks in each paper and a SC/ST
candidate obtains 35% marks in each paper, (this being the qualifying marks for each paper
for General and SC/ST category respectively), this will not necessarily entitle him/her to
claim the right of promotion to the higher post. All candidates who fail to find a place in the
merit list of Successful Candidates to the extent of number of vacancies notified will be
deemed to be unsuccessful in the Competitive Examination. The result shall be subject to
outcome of all court cases pending on various issues like eligibility of inter Regional
Transferees, Regional merit list etc. The result shall also be subject to outcome of any
changes due to re-totalling and verification of marks etc.

The candidature of the candidates is liable to be cancelled at any stage if it is detected
beyond reasonable doubt of having resorted to unfair means in addition to taking other

actions deemed fit or the candidate is found to be ineligible for appearing for the said

examination. This will also apply to all the candidates declared successful in the
examination.

As per the Examination Scheme the facility is provided for candidates for re-totalling
of his/her marks and verification of the fact that all answers written by him/her have been
duly assessed by the examiner and there is no mistake in the totalling of marks. Provision
for re-totalling of marks is available on payment of Rs.5/- per paper. This is to be deposited
by the candidate at the concerned office where he/she is working. Such applications must
be submitted within 15 days from the date of communication of the respective result. Any
application submitted thereafter shall not be entertained. Application is to be submitted
with fees at the office where the candidate is working. The Regional Commissioner
{RO/SRO) should certify the date of payment of fees and the submission of the application.
There is no provision for revaluation of answer papers.

The above details may be brought to the notice of all candidates for their information and
displayed on the notice boards of all the offices in your jurisdiction immediately.

Yours faithfully,

Encl:- As above

(Swagata Rai)

Regional P.F. Commissioner (Exam.)

Subject : Instructions on grant of installment facility to

regarding.

Dear Sir,

Instructions have been issued on grant of installments to the
establishments for liquidating the arrears from time to time in accordance with
the decisions taken by the Central Board of Trustees in its 93 meeting held on
09.10.1982, 129" meeting held on 06.03.1992, 163™ meeting held on
19.08.2003, 166 meeting held on 03.02.2004 and 174‘ meeting held on
23.02.2006.

2. The proposal for further revising the conditions for grant of installments to
the establishments for liquidating the arrears was placed before the Central Board
of Trustees in its 202° meeting held on 13.01.2014 and the Central Board
acceded to the proposal. The following terms and conditions are now prescribed
for allowing the establishments desirous to avail installment facility to liquidate
the arrears in 36 installments:

a) The facility of installment shall be available to both Un-exempted as well as
Exempted Establishments.

b) The facility of installment shall cover unpaid employees as well as
employer’s share of PF contribution, damages, interest.

Page 1 of 3

c) Current contributions and employer’s share shall be paid regularly by 15"
of each month.

d

——

Each installment shall be paid along with interest under Section 7Q of the
month along with current contributions.

€

—

A revolving bank guarantee for an amount equal to one installment shall be
furnished along with the application for installment facility.

f) Post Dated Cheques from the defaulting establishments for the number of
installments shall be obtained for ensuring compliance of terms and
conditions of Installment facility.

——

Contribution in respect of outgoing/ deceased member shall be paid in one
jump sum in the following month itself in addition to the amount of dues
and monthly installment. ,

g

h) The employer shall undertake to pay such damages as may be levied by the
RPFCs concerned and that grant of installment facility is not absolving him
from the payment of statutory dues under Section 14 B and 7Q.

i) In case of dues exceeding Rs. 25 lakhs, the establishment shall furnish in
addition to the revolving bank guarantee covering one installment, an
undertaking that he shall not transfer the immovable property by sale,
lease, gift or any other manner whatsoever during the currency of the
installment facility.

3. Further, the following terms and conditions are prescribed to be satisfied, in
addition to above, by the establishments who desire to avail installment facility
to liquidate the dues in 72 installments:

a) Proposal can only be considered in case of un-exempted
Establishments.

b) If the establishment has earlier availed the installment facility and has

defaulted as per terms/conditions of installment facility, second
application for the same shall not be considered in this regard.

Subject: - Declaration of result of Examination for promotion to the post of Enforcement Officer /

Sir,

Please refer to the notification for conduct of Departmental Competitive Examination for
promotion to the post of EO/AO which was issued on 12.07.2012 (circular no. 222 of website } and the
revised vacancies re-notified vide circular of even number dated 27.01.2014 {circular no. 680 of
website). The result of the said examination is enclosed for circulation to concerned candidates.

2. The result has been prepared based on the Scheme Provisions. As per the EO/AO/SO
Departmental Competitive Examination Scheme, 2009, the General Category candidates who have
scored at least 40% marks in each paper and Reserved category (SC/ST) candidates obtaining 35% marks
in each paper shall be entitled to be arranged in the order of merit in their respective region taking into
account the total marks secured by them in the examination. The number of candidates declared
successful in respect of each Region/ State (erstwhile Region) are only to the extent of vacancies notified
for that Region/ State (erstwhile Region). The fact that a General Category candidate has obtained at
least 40% marks in each Paper and SC/ST candidate obtained 35% marks in each paper will not entitle
him/her to claim the right of promotion to the higher post. All candidates who fail to find a place in the
merit list of Successful Candidates to the extent of number of vacancies notified will be deemed to be
unsuccessful in the examination.

3. On being declared Successful in the Examination, the Candidates from the Regions / States
({Erstwhile Region) will be eligible for consideration for promotion to the post of EO/AO in their
respective Region / States (Erstwhile Region) only.

4. The result shall be subject to outcome of all court cases pending on various issues like
eligibility of Inter Regional Transferees ( SLP NO. 30141-30142 of 2011 filed by Shri M M Thomas and
Ors) , Regional merit list ( SLP No. 22779/ 2013 filed by Shri Rakesh Ranjan & Ors) etc. The result shall
also be subject to outcome of any changes due to re-totalling and verification of marks etc.

5. The successful candidates who have secured the same marks are grouped together indicating
their Ranks. Their seniority will be fixed by the concerned Regional Commissioners on the basis of their
respective seniority in the lower post.

6. The Regional P F Commissioner of Erstwhile Region (State) is requested to take further action
regarding the promotion of such candidates taking note of their eligibility, any court cases, Interim
Orders of the Court if any, cases where disciplinary proceedings are involved etc. All orders for
promotion issued shall clearly specify that such appointment is subject to outcome of the ongoing court
cases,

7. The marks of candidates shall be sent separately. The above details may be brought to the
notice of all candidates for their information and displayed on the notice boards of all offices in your
jurisdiction. Any discrepancies noticed in the details of candidates may be immediately referred to RPFC
(Exam).

scored at least 40% marks in each paper and Reserved category (SC/ST) candidates obtaining 35% marks

merit list of Successful Candidates to the extent of number of vacancies notified will be deemed to be
unsuccessful in the examination.

(Erstwhile Region) will be eligible for consideration for promotion to the post of EO/AO in their
respective Region / States (Erstwhile Region) only.

eligibility of Inter Regional Transferees ( SLP NO. 30141-30142 of 2011 filed by Shri M M Thomas and

also be subject to outcome of any changes due to re-totalling and verification of marks etc.

their Ranks. Their seniority will be fixed by the concerned Regional Commissioners on the basis of their
respective seniority in the lower post.

regarding the promotion of such candidates taking note of their eligibility, any court cases, Interim
Orders of the Court if any, cases where disciplinary proceedings are involved etc. All orders for
promotion issued shall clearly specify that such appointment is subject to outcome of the ongoing court
cases.

notice of all candidates for their information and displayed on the notice boards of all offices in your
jurisdiction. Any discrepancies noticed in the details of candidates may be immediately referred to RPFC

Subject: Judgement of Hon’ble Supreme Court order dated 23.05.2006
in Civil Appeal No. 9523-9524/2013 in the matter of the
Chairman. SEBI Vs. Shri Ram Mutual Fund and another -
regarding

Sir,

Please refer to the above on the cited subject. In this regard, please find
enclosed a copy of the order of Hon’ble Supreme Court dated 23.05.2006 in the
matter of the Chairman SEBI Vs. Shri-Ram Mutual Fund, which is self-explanatory.

2. The gist of the Supreme Court judgment (Chairman SEB] Vs. Sriram
Mutual Fund) cited above is that Mens Rea is not essential ingredient for

contravention of provisions of civil Act.

3. The Supreme Court clearly observed:

“In our opinion, the tribunal has miserably failed to appreciate that by
setting aside the order of the Adjudicating officer the tribunal was setting
8 serious wrong precedent whereby every offender would take shelter of
alleged hardships to violate the provision of the Act. In our opinion mens
rea is not an essential ingredient for contravention of the provisions of a
civil act. In our view, the penalty is attracted as soon as contravention of
the statutory obligations as contemplated by the Act is established and,
therefore, the intention of the parties committing such violation becomes
immateriai, In other word the breach of civil obligation which attracts
penalty under the levy of penalty irrespective of the fact whether the
contravention was made by the defaulter with .any guilty intention or

not”.

4. It is therefore, advised to contest cases relating to section-14B on the

basis of the judgment.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Clarification on the Special Provisions on International Workers — reg.
Sir,

Please refer to subject cited above.

It has been brought to the notice of Head Office by the Addl. CPFC, (AP & Odissa) that
during an interaction/discussion with Employers Forum on the special provisions for the International
Worker, it emerged that following two issues require clarification/clarity in the matter: -

1, The status of an Indian employee visiting a SSA country on posting (deputation) for the
second time. (First time, may even be before the SSA was signed and the second time, duly
obtaining a Certificate of Coverage).

2. The status of Indian employees deputed to non-SSA countries on a short-term posting and
that if they continue to come under the purview of EPF and MP Act, 1952 during the period
of their posting abroad.

In this connection, attention is drawn to point no. 18 & 22 of Frequently Asked Questions
(FAQs) available on our website i.e. http://www.epfindia.com/ vide which the issues raised above
have already been clarified. However, the same are reproduced below for information:

FAQ No. 22 @ on special provisions for International Workers, clarifies that an Indian employee
attains the status of “International Worker” only when he becomes eligible to avail benefits under the
social security programme of other country by virtue of the efigibility gained or going to gain, under
the said agreement on account of employment in a country with which India has signed SSA. He/she
shall remain in that status till the time he/she avails the benefits under EPF Scheme. In other words,
once an IW, always an IW,

Similarly FAQ No. 18 on special provisions for International Workers, clarifies that if an Indian
employee is employed in any covered establishment in India and sent abroad on posting, he is liable to

be a member in India as a domestic Indian employee, if otherwise eligible. He is not an International
Worker.

In view of the above, you are requested to follow the aforesaid guidelines.

Dear Employer(s),

Zonal Training Institute, Employees Provident Fund Organization, North Zone, Faridabad is a unit of
National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security, New Delhi.

Our mission is to provide training programme for the employees/employers of the organization to
make them effective, sound and efficient.

Employees’ Provident Fund & Misc. Provisions Act, 1952 and Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme,
1952 framed are beneficial piece of social welfare legislation aimed at promoting and securing the
well-being of the workers/employees. In order to confer the benefits of the social security scheme to
the workers/employees to the maximum extent within the parameters of law, it is very necessary that
a programme should be organized to impart training to the employers to acquaint themselves with
the various provisions of the Act. The entire Act is directed towards achieving the objective of the Act
by enacting provisions requiring the employers to contribute towards Provident Fund and keep the
Commissioner informed of it by filing on-line returns so that the contributions could be credited to the
account of the subscribers. Further, the training programme will focus on practical exercises on
calculation of various benefits payable in the three scheme viz. Employees, Provident Fund Scheme,
1952, Employees Pension Scheme, 1995 and Employees Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.

With this object, we are conducting a workshop for two days i.e. 13" to 14” Feb, 2014 for the
employers of un-exempted establishments situated in Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh,
Uttar Pradesh and Uttrakhand.

It is, therefore, advised to participate in this workshop for ensuring better compliance of EPF & MP
Act, 1952. For more details, interested employers may contact their respective Regional/Sub-Regional
Office or contact 0129-2297894 for participating in this workshop.

Auto Sweep for A/c No. 22.

Sir,

It has been decided to implement the New Fund Management System
for transfer of funds in respect of A/c No. 21 to corresponding Central Accounts
No.25. The salient features of the fund transfer process under NFMS and brief

procedures to be adopted are furnished for information and follow up action at
field office level:

For A/c No. 21:

1. The existing saving bank account maintained by the field offices for A/c
No. 21 shall be converted into current account. For this purpose a new
account (current account) for A/c No. 21 may be opened. Necessary follow
up with link branch may be initiated in this regard.

ll. There will not be any transfer of subsidy from head office A/e No. 25 to
field office A/c No. 21,

iii. There will not be any specific advice from the field offices to their
respective link branch about the transfer of surplus money to SBI, Mumbai
Main Branch for investment.

iv. All the cheques issued by the field offices in A/c No. 2] would be honoured
by their respective link branches irrespective of the balance available in the
bank account.

Vv. At the end of the day whatever would be the closing balance in A/c No. 21,
(whether debit or credit) would be transferred through auto sweep by the
link branch to A/c No, 25 maintained at SBI, Mumbai Main Branch leaving
NIL balance in A/c No. 21.

V1.

Vil.

Vill.

All the transfers (Debit/Credit) made by the field offices from A/c No. 21
would be effected in corresponding central A/c No. 25 maintained at SBI,
Mumbai Main Branch.

In case there is a deficit (debit balance) as the net balance in A/c No. 25, the
same will be taken care of out of consolidated overdraft limit extended to
EPFO in A/c No. 25 by the SBI Mumbai Main Branch.

Upon coversion of existing SB account No. 21 into current account, the
new current account numbers should be intimated to this office
immediately for reconciliation purpose at Headquarters.

The daily transaction details of A/c No.21 should be furnished in the
prescribed format of NFMS report on monthly basis.

Xx. After opening of current account, the existing saving account will also be in
place till the validity of the last cheque issued from that account has
expired.

For A/c No. 22:

2.

No payments are made from this account. The whole inflow in A/c No. 22 is
transferred to A/c No. 24. Since the receipt in this account is very less, field
offices may issue necessary standing instructions to their link branch to
transfer the amount available in A/c No. 22 on every Saturday to Central
Investment A/c No. 24 by automatic transfer of funds. Thus, Account No. 22
may be put on auto sweep mode for seamless transfer of funds.

All RPFC may kindly ensure compliance of the above fund transfer

process with immediate effect.

Sub: Recovery of excess amount of Pension-reg.
Sir,

A case of fixation of pension at a higher rate than the entitlement was brought to
the notice of the Headquarters. One of the officials, Sh. Sukhdeo Sharma Madhup, an exservice man & SSA of SRO, Muzzafarpur, while working in administration section
processed his own case of pension and calculated pension at higher than entitlement [full
pension after reckoning 33 years of his service whereas he had only 10 years and 10
months service in EPFO]. He got it approved at various levels at SRO, Muzzaffarpur and

RO, Patna including Section Supervisor, APFC (Adm), APFC (Audit), RPFC-Il and RPFC.

HE The case of over drawl of pension came to surface approximately after 4 years
when his seniors drew lesser pension than him. As per rule 9 of the CCS (Pension
Rules), 1972 as adopted by EPFO on 25.10.2008, overpaid pension can be recovered
from the person after a period of 2 years from the date of authorization of pension only
after consultation with the DoPT. In this case, the CAT empowered the CBT to take action

on recovery of excess paid pension, within six months.

a Consequent upon the directions of the Hon’ble CAT, Patna, the Central Board in
its 202"° meeting held on 13.01.2014 approved the proposal for recovery of Rs.

1,29,051/- excess withdrawal of pension & commutation alongwith interest on both.

4. While approving recovery of amount excess drawn alongwith 12% interest the
Central Board during its aforesaid meeting took a serious view of such lacuna in the
system which allowed self processing and calculation of pension. It directed the CPFC to
get the matter investigated and fix responsibility on all the persons who had shown
negligence while handling the case or collusion with the Pensioner. Further, CBT
suggested that a mechanism be devised to ensure that henceforth no person should be
permitted to process calculation of his/her own case of pension, pay and allowances,
arrears or any other financial benefits etc. at any stage. CBT directed that all Punitive
(Civil as well as Criminal) action be taken against, the ex-employees who had

manipulated such over drawl of pension all these years.

a In the above context, it has been decided to review all such cases where, a
person himself/herself processed/ approved/ prepared documents which has resulted at
any stage in an over payment of the dues. Accordingly, all RPFCs/OICs may review all
such cases and fix responsibilities for the lapses incurred. A compliance report on this

issue may be sent by the end of next month.

Yours faithfully,

Ma. a
(V.M. Sharma) —————

SUBJECT:-SUBMISSION OF ANNUAL IMMOVABLE PROPERTY RETURN FOR THE
YEAR 2013 (ENDING 31.12.2013)-BY GROUP ‘A’ OFFICERSUPLOADING THE SAME IN PUBLIC DOMAIN-REGARDING.

Sir,

As per Rule 18(1) (ii) of CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, it is mandatory for all Group

‘A’ officers to submit their Immovable Property return in r/o a calendar year by 31"

January, of the following year.

The Annual Immovable Property Return (AIPR) for the year 2013 will become
due on 01.01.2014. It is requested to advice all Group ‘A’ Officers to submit their AIPR
for the year 2013 (as on 01.01.2014) complete in all respect (including full name and
dated signature) within the stipulated time i.e. latest by 31° January 2014 invariably in
the fomat prescribed enclosed herewith.

It may be ensured that phrases such as “Same as previous year’, “No change”
etc. are not used in the AIPR and full particulars of the Immovable Property
inherited/owned/acquired/gift received or held are furnished in all the columns
specified in the AIPR in terms of Rule 18 of CCS (Conduct) Rules-1964.

As per DoPT’s O.M. No. 11012/112007-Estt.A dated 27.09.2011 and MoLE
Circular No. C-29020/12011-Vig. dated 02.01.2012, vigilance clearance shall be denied
to Group ‘A’ Officers who do not submit their Annual Immovable Property Return by the
time limit i.e. 31.01.2014 in prescribed format.

Letters in Dec-13

Further, appropriate entry regarding late submission/non-submission of AIPRs
should be made in the relevant APARs of the concerned officer in terms of DoPT’s OM
dated 11.07.2011 and No. 2101128/93-Estt (A) dated 20.10.93.

The decisions of Govt. of India in the Circulars/O.M. s cited above and others on
the subject may be brought to the notice of all the officers concerned and they may be
requested to adhere to the time line and format indicated above.

The RPFC-I, In-charge of the Region shail consolidate and forward all the
AIPRs in duplicate alongwith a list of defaulting Officers as on 01.02.2014 latest
by 08.02.2014 to the Head Office and avoid piece meal submission of AIPR’s. A
compliance report on the above may kindly be forwarded via e-mail to:

Subject:

Drive
during
the
month
of

(O1.02.2014 to 28.02.2014).
Sir,
The increasing trend of arrears of Provident Fund and allied dues has become a
matter of great concern. So much so, the performance in recovery of current and arrear dues
is far below the targets fixed by the Headquarters which is not at all appreciable.
2.
The all India Performance for the previous year upto November, 2013 as per Annual
BusinessPlan shows poor pace of recovery which is not acceptable and which is a matter of
great concern.
3.
In order to augment recovery, it is decided that a Special Recovery Drive shall be
carried out during the month of February, 2014 (both un-exempted and exempted sector).
4.
The following polnts shall be kept in mind while conducting the Special Recovery
Drive:
a)
Instructions issued vide this office letter dated 13.07.2012 (placed at website at
S. No. 187) and dated 01.10.2013 (placed at website 51. No. 411) should be
adhered to scrupulously.
b)
Maximum number of Enforcement Officers, as far as practicable, shall be detailed
to
carry
out
such
drive
without
disturbing
other
functional
areas. The
Enforcement Officers before proceeding in the matter shall gather all information
viz. details of bank accounts, details of sundry debtors etc. from the records
available in the office and also from
third
party
source like Income Tax
Department,
Inspector
of
Factories and
Boilers', Inspector
of
Shops and
Establishments, Employees' State Insurance Corporation, Regional Transport
Authorities, Industries and Commerce Departments, Industrial
Estates, Local
Bodies, Co-operative Department, Director of Mining and Geology, Employers'
Associations, Trade Unions etc.

c)
RPFCs,In-charge of Regional Offices/Sub Regional Offices may monitor the
progress of recovery during the currency of the drive on weekly basis and action
plan accordingly may be prepared for following weekrs).
Necessary action
against non-performing
Officers/Officials may be initiated
and informed to
Headquarters.
d)
Vide publicity may be given on such launching of the Special Recovery Drive
through local News Paper,display on the notice boards of the Office prominently,
through Employers' Associations and Trade Unions.
e)
The performance of the Regional Office during the drive in recovery of current
and arrear dues must be reported office wise by the ACCs of the zone in the
Annexures enclosed for un-exempted and exempted sectors separately to Head
Office by 07.03.2014 without fail.
f)
Reports received from Regional Offices and Sub Regional Offices will not be
taken in to cognigance.
S.
The above actions are meant to be taken for meeting the objectives of speedy
recovery of dues and not for any harassment of the employers/ defaulters, which the RPFCs
must ensure.
6.
It is hoped that all out efforts shall be made to make the Special Recovery Drive a
successin its true spirit. Any laxity shall be dealt strongly.
(This issues with the approval
of CPFC)
End: Annexure-I & II.
Yours faithfully,

Sub:- Disbursement of Pension through CBS- Transfer of fund to banks - Corporate
Internet Banking (CINB) Facility.

Ref:- Circular of even no. dated 01.11.2013.

Sir,
Please refer to the above said subject.

It is being reiterated that the undisbursed pension amount e.g. in cases of inactive
accounts in cases of death of pensioners, may be credited in the pension disbursement account
and the pensioners, to whom the amount of pension has not been credited, may be identified by
the link branch. The undisbursed amount may be credited to Account No.10 in T+1 day through
RTGS / NEFT in cases of inter-bank settlement of payment e.g. link branch of PNB to Account
No.10 in link branch of SBI and the undisbursed amount may not be left idle with the link
branch. The pension disbursement account of SBI may be put on auto sweep with A/c No. 10 of
SBI. This system, thus, ensures that reconciliation is immediate and, thereafter, service charge
may be paid promptly to the banks by the field offices.

The banking arrangement between the SBI & EPFO provides for Corporate Internet
Banking (CINB) facility to enable field offices to view real time credit/debit information and
particulars of balance in A/c Nos. 1, 2, 10, 21 & 22. The facility is limited to viewing and
printing of account information only. The same arrangement may be extended to Pension
Disbursement Accounts in SBI and all other Banks to enable the field offices to view the
accounts. The arrangement shall be limited to viewing the account only, without any transaction
facility whatsoever, through the internet banking facility of the respective banks.

(This issues with the approval of FA&CAOQ).

Sub; Non-compifance of Para 72(5) of EPF Scheme, 1952 by Employers - reg.
Sir

With reference to subject cited above, it has been observed that some employers do not
forward the claims submitted to thern by their outgoing employees. This leads to harassment of
such outgoing employees and gives rise to lodging of grievances with EPFO. It is therefore
advised that all Regional Offices and Sub-Regional Offices should sensitise the employers under
their respective jurisdiction to comply with the provisions of Para 72(5) of the EPF Scheme,
1952 where the Employer is duty bound to forward duly filled in and attested claim application
to the respective EPF office within five days of its receipt.

2. It may be made clear to all Employers under your jurisdiction that failure ta comply with
provisions as contained in Para 72(5) will invite penal action as provided under the Act and
Schemes. Wide publicity of these provisions and duty of employers may be given through
seminars, meetings, press notes etc.

3. This is for strict compliance.

(issued with the approval of the CPFC)
Yours faithfully,

Sub:- Review of all cases on EPF staff service matters — Contempt cases
Regarding.

Sir/Madam,

It is observed that in few cases the aggrieved stafffofficer had to file a contempt
petition before the Hon'ble Central Administrative Tribunal as timely action for
implementation of court order was not done. In all such cases, the Regional offices could
have promptly taken action on the directions of the Hon'ble Tribunals. If an appeal was
required to be filed it should have been expedited.

It is a fact that the judicial forums are spread all over the country for facilitating an
option to the aggrieved officials/officers to seek redressal from such forums in the service
matters. Whenever Head quarters advice was required, the same should have been followed
up vigorously so that a situation of facing contempt would not have arisen.

HRM wing at Head Office has already issued a circular dated 07.11.2013 to compile
the All — India position of the cases on service matters. It is again requested to forward the
details of all service matters related cases in the proforma circulated with the said circular.

In view of above, all the Officers-in-charge of the Regional/Sub-Regional
offices/ZV Ds/Vigilance directorate are requested to carry out a review of those cases related
to service matters filed in their respective jurisdiction. After this review, following actions
must be taken immediately:

i. Action on the directions issued by court must be acted upon within the time
frame given in the order or within one month, whichever is earlier.

ui. Application with proper justification for seeking further time. if required in
any case, must be filed through panel advocate, immediately.

Subject: Correction in name of PF Member — Provision in Application Software.
Sir,

IS Division has made a provision in the Application Software for correction in the name,
Father/spouse name and Date of Birth of a Provident Fund member in the WAR release 4.27. In this
regard, the correction in the name, father/spouse name of the member is to be made only on
receipt of joint request of the employee as well as the employer alongwith supporting documents.
The documents may be any of the following:-

(i) PAN Card
(ii) Voters Identity Card
(iii) Passport

(iv) Driving license

(v) ESIC Identity Card

(vi) | Aadhaar Card

(vii) | Bank passbook copy/Post Office Passbook.

(viii) Ration card

(ix) | Any school/education related certificate

(x) Certificate issued by Registrar of Birth & Death.

(xi) Certificate based on the service records of the Central/State Government Organization.

(xii) | Copy of electricity/water/telephone bill in the name of the claimant.

(xiii) Letter from a recognized public authority or public servant verifying the identity and
residence of the member to the satisfaction of the competent authority.

2. In all such cases, correction in the name may be approved by RPFC-II/OIC of SRO or RPFC-IIL
(F&A) of RO, as the case may be.

3. The request for change in the date of birth of a member is to be carried out as per the
guidelines issued by the Head Office vide circular No. Pension/3/8/OR/I/2005 dated 12.12.2006
(placed at ‘office orders & circulars’ at SI. No. 24 of ‘old circulars’).

4, After following the above procedure, DA (Accounts) shall log into the system and carry out
the corrections. The SS (Accounts) will verify and approve the corrections made by the DA

(Accounts). The process flow for executing the change is enclosed for reference.

Yours faithfully,

Subject :- Revised Transfer Claim Process — Claim attestation and verification of member
details on Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP).

Sir,

Please refer to earlier communication on the subject cited above, It may be noted
that under the revised process, the employer is required to carry out following two
activities-

(a) Attestation of claims submitted online by member.

(b) Verification of previous membership details as previous employer in cases where
the claim has been submitted by member through present employer and EPFO
database does not have the previous membership details.

The important guidelines, detailed instructions and frequently asked questions

(FAQs) have been provided on the EPFO website in the link “Online Transfer Claims Portal”
under the category “For employers”.
2. It has been observed that in some cases, the employer has not attested the claims or
verified the member details and the tasks are pending with them. To monitor such pending
tasks, a dashboard has been prepared and the same is available under the login already
provided for “OTCP dashboard”. The username and password for log-in to “OTCP
dashboard” has already sent by mail to all Additional CPFCs earlier.

3. The dashboard has following information in context to the tasks pending with the
employer.

(a) Attestation of claims pending with the employer (Marked as ‘A’ on dashboard)- The
employer has to attest the claim on receipt of signed copy of online claim form from
the member and after its due verification.

(b) Verification of Member details pending with the previous employer- Such cases
occur when the claims have been submitted through the present employer and the
details pertaining to previous establishments are not available in the member master
of EPFO. As regards the pendency of such tasks with the employer, there is a

possibility that the employer is not aware of this task, although e-mails have been sent
to the employers informing about such pending tasks. These details were earlier
obtained in physical form through Form 5/10. A detailed process flow for the same has
already been provided on the portal to the employer. It is reiterated for the
information of field offices that such tasks do not require submission of any signed

copy of the claim form from the member to the employer. This is only a replacement
of earlier Form 5/10. For the purpose of convenience, such tasks have been further

categorized into three categories:-

(i) Claims already attested by the present employer (Marked as ‘B’ on dashboard)-
This is required to be taken up with the employer on topmost priority as the claim
has already been attested by present employer and the same is pending on the
portal due to non-verification of details by the previous employer.

(ii) Claim is yet to be attested by the present employer (Marked as ‘C’ on
dashboard)- This is to be done by the previous employer without delay as such
online claims would be sent to the transfer-out office immediately on attestation
by the present employer.

(iii) Physical claim (Marked as ‘D’ on dashboard)- This is again a top priority category
for the field offices to monitor the tasks pending with the employer as the
physical claims received in the transfer-in office attested by the present employer
have been digitized by the office and are pending on the portal due to nonverification of previous employment details by previous employer on the portal.

4. It is reiterated that the categories (B), (C) and (D) are the verification by the previous
employer of the member details pertaining to previous establishment of member. These
tasks do not require submission of any signed copy of the claim form by the member to the
previous employer as the claim is being attested by the present employer. For better
understanding, it is requested that the field offices should go through the important
guidelines, detailed instructions and frequently asked questions (FAQs) provided for the
reference of the employer. These documents are available on EPFO website through “Online
Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP)” under the category “For employers”.

5. All the field offices are instructed to monitor the tasks pending with the employers
under their jurisdiction and ensure that no task relating to attestation of claims is pending
beyond 15 days and no task relating to verification of member details by previous employer
is pending beyond 7 days.

Sub: Some changes in “EPGiIGMS”
Sir

As you may be aware that grievance redressal portal i.e. EPGiGMS (launched few
years back) is very effective tool for stake holders for getting their grievance escaiated for
their redressal. Till date 5,68,000 nos. of grievances have been received in EPFIGMS, out of
it 5,62,000 (99%) have disposed. A need was felt for incorporating some changes in the
software, for which Head Office is working in close association with NIC. Accordingly
following changes have been effected:

1. Option to export the new grievances in MS-Excel and as PDF.
2. Facility to search a grievance by providing PF number of the subscriber.

3. In Feedback module, sorting facility has been provided on the registration number and
rating columns.
4, Facility of attaching a pdf document to a physical grievance at later stage.

Facility for viewing of all attached documents of a grievance by providing its
registration number.
6. Option of export to MS-Excel and as PDF jn all reports.

Age-wise pendency report as per new pendency periods.

You are requested to get yourself and dealing officers/officials acquainted with
aforesaid changes. Feedback on the functioning of aforesaid changes may please be given
by 27.11.2013.

Subject : Instructions for generating reports for levy of penal damages
under Section 14B and interest under Section 7Q of the EPF &
MP Act, 1952.

Dear Sir,

A report function for levy of Penal Damages and for informing the amount of
payable interest against an establishment has been provided in the new application
software in accordance with Section 14B of the Act read with Para 32A of EPF
Scheme, 1952 and Section 7Q of the Act.

2. The business logic behind the development of the software is as under. There
may be three possible scenarios of Contribution Due and the Belated Payments
made, requiring different treatment under the Act :

a) Scenario-I : Contribution Due before 26.09.2008(C1)
and Belated Payments made_ before
26.09.2008 (P1) ;

b) Scenario-II_ : Contribution Due after 26.09.2008(C2)
and Belated Payments made after
26.09.2008(P2);

c) Scenario-III : Contribution Due prior to 26,09.2008(C1)
but Belated Payments made on/after
26.09.2008(P2).

3. The combination of Contributions Due and Belated Payments made before
and after 26.09.2008 gives rise to the following rates of Penal Damages applicable
to each combination : 1)

a) Ci+Pi_ : Pre-Revised Rates of Penal Damages
b) C2+P2 : Revised Rates of Penal Damages

c) C1l+P2 : Pre-Revised Rates on Cl(i.e. Contributions Due
before 26.09.2008) and at Revised Rates on
C2(i.e. Contributions Due after 26.09.2008)

4. The same has been deployed through the application war version 4.22 on
03.10.2013.The reports can be generated from two different modules as detailed
below :

i) Establishment Module> Reports (for migrated and new Challan)
ii) Data Migration Module >> Reports (for legacy —- Challan not migrated)
From the Establishment Module, the following reports can be generated:

a) List of establishments against which penal damages is to be
levied :

> This report gives a list of such establishments against which penal
damages are to be levied. Such establishments are also required to
pay the interest under Section 7Q of the Act.

> There is a option in this module for the users to generate the report
for Establishments under each Enforcement Group and for a
particular period.

> In case the “All” is selected the report will be generated for all Challans
having presentation date from 01.04.1996 to the system date.

> The report can be generated for any selected period but not prior to
01.04.1996.

> The report can be generated for a range of probable damages and
amount of interest.

> After generating the list for all the Enforcement Groups and ranges,
the data shall be verified from the respective penal damages file to
check the period till which the damages are already levied / notices
already issued so that another notice is not issued for the same period

INTERACTION WITH THE REPRESENTATIVES OF EXEMPTED ESTABLISHMENTS

Date: 10™ October 2013
Time: from 03:00 PM onwards
Venue: EPF Headquarters

Setting the tone of the meeting, at the very outset CPFC clarified that the basic idea
behind the interactive session was to provide a common platform for the exempted PF
Trusts where they can periodically get together to discuss matters of common interest
and mutually benefit from the experiences of each other. EPFO being the big brother of
all such Trusts it was thought natural to take lead in this matter.

Issues arising out of the interaction are listed below: -
CLAIMS
Annexure K

Several representatives raised the issue of delay in receipt of Annexure K from RPFCs.
Annexure K contains vital details of members whose P F Account balance has been
transferred to some exempted Trust or to the RPFCs. In the absence of Annexure
K, the Trusts are unable to credit the sum so received in the Account of respective
members of the Trust. This leads to avoidable grievances. ACC(IS) and FA & CAO
assured early solution to this problem in the new digitalized environment through
application software.

EPS claims

Several representatives brought to focus the issue of inordinate delay in settlement of
EPS claims by the RPFCs. They admitted improvement in the services of EPFO in the
recent past, but expressed disappointment in the area of settlement EPS claims in Form10D/10C for pension /withdrawal benefit/scheme certificate. They conveyed that the
Trust being the custodian of PF money of their members promptly settle their PF claims,
but EPS claims being in the domain of RPFCs get delayed and on many occasions even
frequent persuasions fail to yield quick results.

Interest Rate

A significant revelation of this interactive session was that several Trusts have been
declaring higher rate of interest to be credited to members’ account compared to
statutory rate of interest declared by the EPFO volitionally, based on the financial health
of the Trusts. CPFC desired that such Trusts should be honoured for their noble
endeavours and we must learn from their best practices.

Subject: Implementation of New Funds Management System(NFMS) in respect
of A/c No. 1 & 10.

* It has been observed that a few field offices have not been implementing
the New Fund Management System(NFMS) for online transfer of funds, whether debit or
credit, by auto-sweep from A/c No. 1 & 10 to A/c No. 5 & 11 respectively on a daily
basis. As a result, funds have remained idle in the link branches of the SBI and the same
could neither be invested in time nor transferred to meet the liabilities of payments.
Accordingly, all field offices may take up the matter with their respective link branches
to ensure the following:

1. A NIL balance in A/c No. 1 & 10 at the end of the day is maintained by the

link branch of the SBI.

Ll. If there is a delay in transfer of credit balance by the link branches, a penal
interest claim shall be filed immediately with the link branch as per the
agreement between the CBT, EPF and the SBI. Presently, the interest @9.75%
for A/c No. | and 9.25% for A/c No. 10 is to be claimed for delay in transfers.

il. A monthly NFMS Return shall be sent to Head Office through e-mail at
epfobanking@gmail.com in the prescribed NFMS program. This return by email may NOT be followed by a hard copy by the field offices.

iv. A register may also be maintained for monitoring the closing balance every
day for A/c No. 1, 2, 10, 21 and 22 by RPFC-II, In-charge of SROs and RPFCIl(F&A) posted in the ROs.

V. RPFC-II(F&A) has an important role in supervising fund transfer so that funds
do not remain idle with the bank. All RPFC-II(F&A) are requested to submit a

Sub:- No enabling provision in EPS, 1995 therefore no deficiency in service — Order of
the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Haryana, Panchkula [R.K,
Verma Vs. APFC (Pension) & others (Complaint No. 99/12)).

Sir,

AS you are aware that there 1s no provision in the EPS, 1995 for restoration of commuted
pension, and therefore once a pensioner opted for commutation, such pensioner is entitled only
for balance pension on monthly basis

The above contention has been accepted by the State Consumer Disputes Redressal
Commission, in its order dated 02-09-2013 (copy enclosed).

In this Order, tt is stated that —

“There is no enabling provision in the rules (of EPS, 1995) for restoration of commuted
pension. The complainant cannot take the benefits of Central Government Employees Pension
Rules, which are no! applicable in this case, There is no provision of restoration of commuted
pension in Employees Pension Scheme, 1995, which are applicable to employees of Public
Sector Undertaking under which they get pension. Thus, without there being any provision in the
rules for restoration of pension, the opposite parties cannot be termed as deficient in service.”

Accordingly, in similar appropriate legal disputes, {he judgment may be utilised.

Sub: - Contribution on salary exceeding the statutory limit under Para 11(3) of
the EPS' 9S

Reference: 1. Circular No. Pen/4(2)96/SLP/Vol, V/16598 dated 26/06/04
2. Letter No. Pen.4(38)96/WB/59867 dated 01/12/04
3, Circular No, Pen/Misc/2006/Vol.| dated 25/04/06
4. Circular No. Pension/Misc./2005/65836 dated 22/11/06

Kind reference is invited to the headquarters circulars cited above
wherein the issue of contributing on a pay exceeding the statutory limit under
Para 11(3) of the Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995 has been the point of
consideration.

2. This matter has been receiving attention in headquarters and the
following significant facts have emerged in the analysis:

{i} Every option for contribution on higher wages is putting the Pension Fund
under strain on account of the higher payout obligations arising out of It.
The payout is disproportionate to the contributions received in respect of
cases where there is an option for contribution on higher wages.

(ii) Currently the Pension Fund is running at an overall deficit as per Actuarial
valuations and it would be unwarranted to increase the deficit by
accepting options for contribution on higher wages knowing fully well that
benefit payout in such cases are detrimental to the viability of the Find.

(iii] Members contributing on higher wages draw benefits disproportionate to
the contributions, even given the fact that in their case the contributions
are on higher salaries. In effect the poor members are subsidizing the
benefits for the relatively richer members, This is a most undesirable and
repugnant situation that needs to be corrected immediately,

3. In view of the foregoing, it has been decided that henceforth and until
further orders no permission will be accorded for contribution on higher wages
under EPS.

4. As may be evident under EPS there is no contribution payable separately.
Under Para 3 of the EPS, from and out of the contributions payable by the
employer in each month under section 6 of the Act, the employer shall remit a
part of contribution representing 8.33% of the employees’ pay to the EPS,
Accordingly, the option to contribute on a pay exceeding statutory limit is
available to a member only under Para 26(6) of the Employees Provident Fund
Scheme, 1952 and not under Para 11(3) of the EPS.

5, Para 26(6) of the EPF Scheme 1952 provides that the contribution on
higher wages would be permitted by an officer not below the rank of APFC on the
joint request of the employer and employee. The option for contribution on
higher wages to the EPS would have to be regulated under this Para, Accordingly,
in all cases where joint requests from employer and employee preferring option
for contribution on higher wages are received under Para 26[{6), the permission
for contribution on higher wages may be accorded subject to the condition that
contribution to the EPS on higher wages would not be allowed and shal! be
limited to wage ceiling only, The reason for declining option for contribution on
higher wages to EPS, that have been detailed in paragraph 2 above should also be
clearly mentioned in the option acceptance letter/order,

[This issues with the approval of the CPFC]

Yours faithfully,
(Chandramauli Chakraborty)

Subject:- Expeditions settlement of Transfer claims:- Regarding.

Reference:~Head Office Letter No. IS/Project I- Transfer claims/ dated
03.10.2013

Sir,

The objective of social security to get sufficient P.F. accumulations and old age
pension cannot be met unless EPF members get their P.F. account transferred after
changing jobs. Erstwhile system involved a lot of hassles and paper movement from one
office to another and caused lot of delays and grievances regarding settlement of
transfer claims. Transfer claim settlement process was re-engineered and members were
given option to apply at transfer out office i.e. previous office after attestation by
previous employer. Crediting members account in computer system has been made
faster by direct credit through NEFT in computer system itself. It has been reported that
the beta version of software is functioning reliably. However, to attain better efficiency in
expeditious settlement of claims, following action are required at field offices: -

1. Employers be made aware by e-mail or otherwise, about new faster procedure
of sending transfer claims through previous employer in previous office
(Transfer out office) where previous accounts of member is maintained.

2. Take appropriate measures to familiarise the staff and officers about revised
processes for settlement of transfer claims circulated vide letter No |S/Project
i- Transfer claims/dated 3/10/2013. However revised process is summarised in
Annexure-{ to reiterate important points for better understanding and smooth
implementation of the process.

3. For online submission of transfer claims the availability of member’s details in
member master is essential. In some isolated cases members are not able to
submit claims online due to non availability of member’s details in member
Master. This also create hurdle in the digitization of claims at transfer in offices.
The following actions be taken by all ROs & SROs to update members master to
remove blockades in submission of transfer claims online.

Annual accounts of exempted establishments need to be updated so
that members who have left the exempted establishment in pre ECR
period can also submit claims online. Some exempted establishments
give a separate PF Code No. to its employees in respect of PF
maintained with trust. E-mails be sent to such exempted
establishments with a request to guide members to quote A/c number
maintained with EPFO instead of A/c number of trust for online
submission of claim. Our system recognizes the PF No. allotted by us
only.

Wherever annual accounts of establishments have been processed
without taking into account its annual returns (Form3A/6A) for some
technical reason for some period /years, the members who joined and
left during this period are not able to submit claims online due to non
availability of member’s data. Hence actions be taken to update
members annual accounts with contribution.

Wherever member’s data has not been released at the time of data
migration, action be taken to release the same so that members can
avail the facility of online submission of claims.

In cases of joining a new establishment recently, the members are
deprived from submission of online claims if establishment has not
submitted the ECR or submitted ECR but the same has not been
uploaded/ reconciled in application software. Hence timely upload and
reconciliation of ECRs in application system be ensured at ROs and SROs

It is expected that above actions would be taken on top priority to enable the EPF
members to derive maximum advantage of the revised process of online claim submission
and faster claim settlement.

Sir,
Please refer to the above said subject.

The advance payment of pension may be remitted to the bank a
day before credit of pension. All transfers to non-SBI banks may be
effected through the RBI operated RTGS/NEFT systems of payment.
The transfer to the pension disbursement account of SBI may be
effected on the SBI’s CBS platform only. The adoption of such an
electronic mode of transfer of money for disbursement of pension
would cut down of float available with the bankers and EPFO can earn
interest of up to ten days with the new arrangement in place.

The undisbursed pension amount e.g. in cases of inactive
accounts in cases of death of pensioners, may be credited in the
pension disbursement account and the pensioners, to whom the
amount of pension has not been credited, may be identified by the link
branch. The undisbursed amount may be credited to Account No.10 in
T+i day through RTGS / NEFT in cases of inter-bank settlement of
payment e.g. link branch of PNB to Account No.10 in link branch of SBI
and the undisbursed amount may not be left idle with the link branch.
The pension disbursement account of SBI may be put on auto sweep
with A/c No. 10 of SBI. This system, thus, ensures that reconciliation
is immediate and, thereafter, service charge may be paid promptly to
the banks by the field offices.

All RPFCs are directed to ensure that pension payment is made
on the last working day of every month through the CBS platform
only. It is again reiterated that any new PPO shall be issued only after
obtaining CBS account number from the applicant. The responsibility
for implementation of transfer of funds in respect of pensioners shall
lie with RPFC-II, In-charge of the Sub Regional Offices and RPFCII(F&A) of the Regional Offices respectively.

Subject:- Specimen signatures of Authorised Signaories for settlement of
Claims - Regarding.

Sir,

It has come to the notice of the undersigned that the field offices are
rejecting the physical claims received in the office on the pretext that the claims
have been attested by the authorized signatories other than those registered for

their digital signatures with EPFO.

2. It is reiterated that the digital signature certificates of the authorized
signatory are for the purposes of attestation of the digital claim by the employer. In
addition to attestation of the digital claim, the same authorized signatory can also
verify the physical claims received through the employer. In such situation, the
physical signature of the authorized signatory will be verified from the latest

specimen signature given for the particular authorized signatory.

3. In case the employer has not authorized any signatory for signing the online
claims, the physical claims will be signed by the existing authorized signatory and

their signature will be verified from existing specimen signature card.

4. In case the employer has authorized few digital signatories (not more than 3)
in addition to existing authorized signatory, all such authorized signatories may also
attest the physical claims and the signature will be verified from the specimen

signature card of the respective authorized signatory.

Ss. In a situation where the digital signatory was also authorized earlier to sign
physical claims, the latest specimen signature will be verified in case same person

verifies the claim by putting his physical signature.

Yours faithfully,

(Sanjay Kumar)

Sub: Declaration of Productivity Linked Bonus (P.L. B.) for the year 2012-2013.
Sir,

The Central Government, under Section 5D(7) of the Employees’ Provident Funds &
Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 has conveyed its approval to the extension of the existing
Productivity Linked Bonus Scheme 1998-2004 (Revised) for the year 2012-2013 vide their
letter No A-26022/1/1994-SS.1 dated 07" October 2013.

2. Accordingly, the Central Provident Fund Commissioner is pleased to approve the
payment of the Productivity Linked Bonus for the year 2012-2013 for 60(Sixty) days in
all the offices of EPFOQ. The bonus of 60 days has been assessed on the basis of
Performance Report forwarded by the field offices in compliance to Head Office letter dated
09.09.2013. The payment of bonus is to be released before Puja Festival, to all Group ‘C’, ‘D’
and Group ‘B’ (Non-Gazetted) employees.

3, The terms and conditions governing payment of P.L.B. will be as per the instructions
issued by the Government of India for payment of the bonus to the employees in Central
Government departments from time to time. However, the quantum of bonus may be
assessed as per the following formula circulated vide Govt. of India, Ministry of Finance O.M.
No. 14(1) E.Co-ord.1/2004 dated 30.9.2004.

= (AVERAGE EMOLUMENTS) X (NUMBER OF DAYS OF BONUS)
30.4 X (AVERAGE NUMBER OF DAYS IN A MONTH)

4. The maximum amount of bonus will be restricted to the amount admissible to those
drawing emoluments of Rs.3,500/- per month. The bonus in respect of the employees drawing
emoluments of more than Rs.3,500/- per month will be calculated as if the emoluments were
Rs.3,500/- per month.

5. The term ‘emoluments’ occurring in these orders will include Basic Pay, Personal Pay,
Special Pay, Deputation (Duty) Allowance and Dearness Allowance, but will not include other
Allowances, such as HRA, CCA Special Compensatory (Remote locality) Allowance, Bad Climate
Allowance, Children Education Allowance and Interim Relief etc.

6. The expenditure incurred for payment of bonus may please be debited from the budget
head “Productivity Linked Bonus.”

Yours faithfully,

(Sanjay Kumar)
Financial Advisor & Chief Accounts Officer

Subject:- Declaration of Result of the Departmental Competitive Examination for
promotion to the post of Hindi Translator — Grade II held from 18 19" July,
2013.- Reg

Sir/ Madam,

Please refer to the circular number Exam/ 4(1)2013/27 dated 15.04.2013 ( Website
circular no. 31) according to which the Departmental Competitive Examination for promotion to
the post of Hindi Translator — Grade II was held on 18" — 19" July, 2013.

2. The FINAL MERIT LIST OF SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATES is enclosed as
“ANNEXURE ‘A’ and the Marklist of all appeared Candidates, Roll Number wise, alongwith
the marks in all three Papers and Total Marks is placed at ANNEXURE ‘B”. No separate
marklist will be issued to the candidates and hence the candidates may be intimated about the
result by the concerned RPFC. The result is subject to outcome of re-totalling and confirmation of
eligibility of the candidates by the appointing authority.

3. Candidates can apply for re-totalling of their marks and verification of the fact that all
answers written by them have been duly assessed by the examiner and there is no mistake in the
totalling of marks. Provision for re-totalling of marks is available on payment of Rs.5/- per
paper. This is to be deposited by the candidate at the concerned office where he/she is working.
Applications must be submitted within one month from the date of announcement of the result.
Any application submitted thereafter shall not be entertained. Application (in prescribed format)
is to be submitted with fees at the office where the candidate is working. The Officer In-charge
