Subject : Compliance under the EPF & MP Act, 1952 in respect of
the employees engaged by or through contractors.
Sir,

A number of complaints are received by the organization on non-extension of social
security benefits in the form of provident fund, pension and insurance as envisaged under the
Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 and Schemes framed there
under especially to the casual, contractual and outsourced employees working in different
establishments, Government Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous bodies, both Central
and State. Accordingly, the very purpose of this social legislation is defeated.

2. The word employee has been defined to mean any person who is employed for wages in
any kind of work, manual or otherwise, in or in connection with the work of an establishment
and who gets his wages directly or indirectly from the employer, and includes any person
employed by or through a contractor in or in connection with the work of the establishment.
The Act does not differentiate between casual, contractual and regular employees.

3. Various Government Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous bodies, both Central
and State, outsource the activities like watch-ward, housekeeping, data-entry etc. to different
agencies and contractors and the persons engaged by such agencies and contractors to execute
the above activities are not extended due benefits of provident fund, pension and insurance.
This increases the number of grievances to the organization.

Page 1 of 3

4. Paragraph 30(3) of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 provides that it shall
be the responsibility of the principal employer to pay both the contribution payable by himself in
respect of the employees directly employed by him and also in respect of the employees
employed by or through a contractor and also administrative charges. This is not enforced in
true spirit by various Government Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous bodies, both
Central and State. Wherever enforced, there is no proper scrutiny at the time of the payment of
their bills as to whether the agencies and contractors are depositing contributions due from
them under the Act and the Schemes framed thereunder which is commensurate with the
wages paid to such out sourced staff.

5. Instances have come to notice that the placement agencies and security agencies, which
provide guards and other personnel to Government Departments, Undertakings and
Autonomous Bodies often take employer's contribution on full wages from these employers and
then bifurcate the wages of the personnel provided by them in to basic wages and various
other allowances which do not form part of basic wages to evade the provident fund. This
diversion of residual employer's contribution tantamount to pilfering of provident fund money.
Thus, Governments Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies, which settle the
periodic bills of agencies and contractors, unwillingly become a party to this pilferage.

6. Time has come to work on such issues of concern and to converse and inform these
Government Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies about their role while
engaging the various agencies and contractors and while settling their monthly bills with
respect to deployment of such personnel.

7. In this background, all the Regional Provident Fund Commissioners In-Charge of
Regional/Sub Regional Offices are advised to start a dialogue with the Government
Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies functioning under your jurisdiction about
their duties and responsibilities while engaging personnel for watch-ward, housekeeping, dataentry etc. through various agencies and contractors to check such pilferage of provident fund
monies. The Officers-In-Charge are also advised to collect the details of personnel engaged
through the various agencies and contractors from these Government Departments,
Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies and check with the records available in their own offices
about such agencies and contractors. Wherever pilfering of provident fund money is noticed,
immediate action shall be initiated against the erring agencies and contractors to check such
unhealthy practices harming the interest of the workers.

8. The Regional Provident Fund Commissioners In-Charge of Regional/Sub Regional Offices
are advised to issue notices to the Government Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous
Bodies functioning under your jurisdiction for arresting such unfair practices, which various

Sub: Fraudulent withdrawal from the Account of EPFO by furnished
forged statutory returns

Sir,

Recently this office has come across cases of fraud wherein the PF
money has been withdrawn through fictitious claims.

ia The investigation has revealed that the fraud was committed mainly in
respect of those establishments where remittances had not been received for
many years, records not updated and the establishment had not submitted
statutory returns. Further, no pre-coverage/post coverage inspections were
carried out of the establishments and no claims were received or settled since
long.

3: The investigation has revealed that the fraudsters had submitted
forged/fabricated returns viz. Form-3A/6A, 9(R), Specimen Signature Cards
and thereafter, submitted fictitious claims in the name of original members or
non members. Instances have also come into notice where returns were
submitted after submission of claims. The claims were settled by putting
Pressure on Dealing Hands/office by all possible means. In all these cases the
amount settled had been sent through NEFT in the Bank Accounts opened
with forged identity. The major cause of such fraud has been the non
inspection of establishments and acceptance of forged statutory returns,

particularly Specimen Signature Card of Authorized Signatory, blindly
without putting them to verification.

a. It is a known fact that a fraud is aided or facilitated when there is non
adherence to MAP/Head Office instructions including those relating to
updating of Annual Accounts, Specimen Signature Cards, Form-9, Form-5
and maintenance of statutory returns viz. Form 3A/6A, furnished by the
establishment. In the aforesaid cases the fraud was committed in respect of
Inoperative Accounts.

9 All the field offices are requested to keep special watch and remain
alert while processing the claims specially pertaining to closed establishment
or establishment in respect of whom remittance have not been received for
years. The instructions given in the matter of processing INOPERATIVE
ACCOUNTS should be followed strictly.

6. The contents of the circular may be conveyed to all the officials in your
region to prevent occurrence of similar instances. Further, direction may be
issued to ensure strict compliance of the procedure laid down in the Manual
of Accounting Procedure and instructions issued by the Head Office from
time to time on the subject matter.

(This is issued with the approval of CPFC)

Yours faithfully

Subject:- Release of Beta version of Software for Revised process for settlement of

Transfer Claims.
Reference:- (i) Head Office Letter No. IS/Project I- Transfer claims/ dated 25.07.2013
(ii) Head Office Letter No. 1S/Project I- Transfer claims/ dated 25.07.2013
Sir,

As you are aware that software for online transfer claim settlement is under
development for some time. As informed earlier by communication from the Head Office letter
No. IS/Project-I-Transfer claims/ dated 25-07-2013, the new process will have the following
fundamental changes for settlement of transfer claims -

The claims can be submitted through previous employer or present employer.
There would be no movement of physical papers between the EPFO offices.

c. In addition to the physical form, the members can submit the claims online through
digital mode.

2. The Beta version of the software is being released today to commemorate 144" Birth
Anniversary of the Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi whose entire life was dedicated to
provide better service to the mankind particularly to the under-privileged. In line with vision
and aspiration of the Father of the Nation, EPFO strives to provide best service to the workers
of organized sector particularly to the workers who are not so well paid.

3. In order to enable the software to function to the best of its potential, the transfer claim
form was modified and released by Hon’ble LEM on 04/07/2013. The new transfer claim form
has been made mandatory with effect from 15-09-2013.

4, It may be noted that there are minimal changes made in the Application Software
functional in field offices. It is hereby directed that all transfer claim forms now received in the
modified format be processed using the beta version of the software being released today. The
software also allows eligible EPF members to file their claim online. Such online application
should also be processed as test case under close supervision and any problem identified during
the process may be immediately reported to Head Office to Mr. Ravi Kant, RPFC-I(IS) for
improvement in the software. A formal launch of the modified software will be made on the
basis of the feedback received from you.

5. The entire process flow has already been explained to the officials deputed from field
offices for training on the ‘Revised process of transfer claim settlement’ held at NATRSS from
23" September to 25" September, 2013. For ready reference, the process flow is annexed to
the letter.

6. Apart from the above process flow detailed at Annexure, the changes in the Manual of
Accounting Procedure for creation of new roles on the basis of modified process will follow.

Yours faithfully,

Subject: Recovery of Arrear Dues.
Sir,
This is with reference to the detailed and comprehensive instructions issued vide letter No. RRCIII/13(228)Circular/2012/4149 dated 19.06.2012 on the above subject (placed at S|.No.187 in ‘Office
Orders and Circulars segment for the year 2012-13 in the Official Website).

2. It is to reiterate that the increasing trend of arrears of Provident Fund allied dues has become
a matter of great concern. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India, which recently conducted

' Performance Audit of the Organisation for the period from 2006-07 to 2010-11, observed that the
contribution due ad arrears to be received from the establishments has been mounting on one hand and
recovery thereof shows a downward trend on the other.

3. In the said directions, targets were also set in the area of recovery of current and arrear
demand in Immediately Realizable Category as 100% and 80% respectively. It was also instructed that
independent dossiers shall be maintained in respect of each defaulting establishment having an arrear of
Rupees One Lakh and above and which shall contain all relevant points for effective review and

monitoring.

4. The jurisdiction of review of dossiers of defaulting establishments was prescribed as under:
Designation of Officers : Jurisdiction
Additional CPFCs (Zones) : Defaults exceeding Rs. 50 lakhs
RPFC-I, In-Charge of Region : Defaults of Rs. 10 lakhs to Rs. 50 lakhs

RPFC-II, In-Charge of Compliance & Recovery/RPFC-II,

In-Charge of Sub-Regional Offices Defaults of Rs. 5 lakhs to Rs. 10 lakhs

Assistant Provident Fund Commissioners In-Charge of : Defaults upto Rs. 5 lakhs
Compliance & Recovery

Page 1 of 2

5. It is seen that there has not been effective review and monitoring of recovery of current and
arrear demand in accordance with the instructions issued vide this office letter dated 19.06.2012.
Resultantly, the performance of recovery of current and arrear demand of the organization for the year
2012-13 is not very much encouraging. Even the performance of the current year (2013-14) for the
period from April to June 2013 does not show any substantial progress. As on 31% March 2013, there is
an outstanding of Rs.4157.40 crore to be recovered from the defaulting establishments.

6. As recovery of arrears is directly linked to service delivery involving settlement of claims and
updation of member accounts, all the Regional Provident Fund Commissioners In-Charge of Regional
and Sub-Regional Offices are once again advised to draw effective action plan and to ensure prompt
initiation of recovery actions to augment recovery. Cases where Courts have granted stay, efforts shall
be taken to vacate the stay. Similarly, in case of establishments which are under liquidation, appropriate
claims be filed with the Official Liquidator and the cases be regularly monitored. Wherever installment
facilities are granted, proper watch shall be there for regular receipt of installments.

7. The action plan so drawn shall be sent to Head Office through Additional CPFC of the Zone within
15 days and the review of performance in this area at Head Office will base on the said action plan.

8. The instructions as contained in the above circular shall be followed in true spirit. It may be
ensured that while executing the Revenue Recovery Certificates and recovering the Provident Fund and
allied dues, cost, processing fees including all expenses incurred thereof etc. are recovered in
accordance with the instructions contained in Head Office Circular No. RRC/28(3)03 dated 17.02.2004
(copy enclosed).

Sir,

The National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) is conducting a five
days Outbound Training Programme on “Leadership & Team Building” scheduled from 21% October
~25" October, 2013 at Portblair.

This outbound training programme aims at team building from the leadership perspective and to
underline the importance of individuai in a team. The main objective of the course is to make the
individual aware of dynamics and constants of team building in varied work situations and to enable the
participants to achieve the common task.

The training will include adventure activities in addition to management exercises and classroom
sessions. Trekking, adventure sports, team exercises, survival exercises etc. will be a part of the
training. Only those officers who are physically fit and capable of enduring extensive physical activity
need apply for the programme.

Nominations may please be sent to the undersigned by fax or e-mail, preferably before
07" October 2013. NATRSS wil! circulate the list of shortlisted participants on 11™ October 2013.
Detailed itinerary of the programme alongwith instructions for participation will be communicated to
shortlisted officers individually. The selected officers may be relieved accordingly.

The reporting and relieving point for the programme will be SRO Portblair. NATRSS will make
travel arrangements after report of duty at the reporting point. The officers will have to make their own
travel arrangements to & fro the reporting point. NATRSS will also coordinate board and lodge at the
training venue. The actual expenses towards the same will be borne by individual officers out of daily
allowance admissibie under the rules.

The programme is designed to be especially beneficial for the officers performing leadership roles.
The officers in the cadre of ACCs/RPFC —I are, therefore, encouraged to participate in the
programme.

Sub: Submission of Revised Estimates for the year 2013-14 and Budgel Estimates
for the year 2014-15 in respect of Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, 1952
(including Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995) and Employees' Deposit
Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.
In accordance with the provisions regarding budget contained in Para 58 of
the EPF Scheme 1952, on probable Receipts and Expenditure relating to the
Administration of the Funds, the Revised Estimates for the year 2013-14 and the
Budget Estimates for the year 2014-15 of the EPF Organisation, based on the
actual Income & Expenditure upto 30th September 2013 (i.e. from 1.4.2013 to
30.9.2013), are to be prepared and placed before the Central Board of Trustees,
EPF for the consideration and approval in this financial year.
2.
The budgetary exercise should not be treated as mere routine exercise and
it should receive the personal attention of the Regional P.F. Coi nmissicner-I and
the OIC of SRO for its correctness and timely submission. On the part of the RPFC-I1
(F&A), it should be treated as a vital function for the respective Region including
for the SROs and he should devote his personal attention in assisting the Regional
Commissioner ii;)-charge of the Region. Efforts should be made to frame the
Revised Estimates for 2013-14 in such a manner that there may not be any
necessity for Re-appropriation/ Additional Funds in the last month of the financial
year.
3.
The NATRSS is treated as an independent unit and separate funds are
allotted. to meet its own expenditure and the Zonal Training Institutes (ZTL;), Sub-ZTI
(Shillong) working under them. As such, Director, NATRSS, shaU submil budget
proposal separately for NATRSS including ZTIs and the Sub-ZTI.
LAIdget for
Deputy Director, Vigilance (NZ) may be included in the proposal o NATR5.S.

4.
RPFC (ASD), Head Office is also required to submit the proposal of Revised
Estimate 2013-14 & Budget Estimates 2014-15 in respect of Head Office including
the proposal of National Data Centre, Bhavishya Nidhi Enclave and Bhavishya
Nidhi Bhawan regarding requirement of funds under the budget head "Petty
Works & Maintenance of Office Building and Staff Quarters "which will be at the
disposal of Chief Engineer, PFD, Head Office.
5.
Similarly, the EPF Appellate Tribunal shall be treated as a separate unit and
separate funds are to be allotted to meet its own expenditure. As such, Registrar,
EPF Appellate Tribunal shall submit budget proposal separately.
6.
The following guidelines may please be kept in mind while formulating the
Revised Estimates for 2013-14 and Budget Estimates for 2014-15: -
(i)
One single proposal is required to be prepared in respect of a Region as a
whole by consolidating the proposals of Regional Office and the SubRegional Offices. RPFC-In-Charge of the Region as well as RPFC-II (F&A)
may, therefore, consult the OICs of SROs under their control immediately to
ensure that there is no delay in transmission of the requisite information to
their office. The Revised Estimates for 2013-14 and Budget Estimates for
2014-15 for the offices of Addl. CPFCs (Zones) and Permanent Inquiry
Officers, Zonal Audit Parties and Deputy Directorates (Vigilance) may
include any new requirements, if any, other than the routine items like Pay &
Allowances, TA, Stationary, Phone etc. to the Regional Offices or NATRSS
whichever is concerned, where these offices are situated, which in turn, will
include the same in the consolidated budget proposal of the Region.
(ii)
For enable us to assess the amount of contributions estimated as receivable
during the year 2013-14 (Revised Estimates) and in 2014-15 (Budget
Estimates), the details of contributions may be given in statements as
prescribed in Annexure - BT/A. The figures of Income, Contribution, and
Expenditure may be in Rupees format only. If, there is a great variation the
justification may be given.

RECORD OF DECISIONS OF THE MEETING OF ACC
(ZONES) HELD ON 06-09-2013
(CONFERENCE ROOM, EPF HEADQUARTERS, NEW DELHI)
1.
The list of participants is at Annexure A.

2.
CPFC, in his inaugural address welcomed all the officers and thanked them for
arriving at a short notice. He made the following observations:

i)
ACCs are performing very important job. They should work as extended arms of
CPFC. To that extent, they should be detached from the field and should
consider themselves as part of policy formulation and supervisory wing.
ii)
The tours of the ACCs to offices of ROs & SROs are not structured. The ACCs
are not sending their tour notes. Some indicative tour notes are being given.
iv)
Despite a written and clear manual, different systems were being followed by
different offices to do the same thing. It was surprising that there is no system
which accounts for every entry of an article into the office.
v)
The staff of EPFO is highly educated and if given the right and regular
directions, it can perform much better than it was doing at present.
vi)
The Officer and staff consider the EPFO as a rich Organisation. They do
not have enough money value in mind while taking decisions. Further, the
financial instruments received in this office are even not put to use for day
and months together.
vii)
The ACCs need to be innovative and should think of at least one area. The
success story can then be adopted in other zones.

3.
CUSTOMER SERVICE DIVISION

On this topic deliberations took place and following decisions were taken: –

i.
Every complaint, coming by any mode shall be compulsorily registered in
EPFIGMS. Whether the complaints are being registered or not shall form
part of periodical inspection.
ii.
Disposal/Redressal of complaints should be compulsorily done within 30 days.
iii.
Analysis of the grievance settlement indicates that almost 43% people are
not satisfied with the redressal of grievances. Feedback on this issue, as
received from members is to be personally monitored by the Zonal ACCs.
Zonal ACCs may coordinate with ACC (CSD) in this regard.
iv.
Quantitative and qualitative disposal of grievances shall be reviewed by ACCs
in their tour inspection note. The work of PROs in EPF field offices must be
looked into so that stakeholders get better service. The instructions issued
vide circular number 322 (office circulars 2013-14) to be adhered.

Subject: Furnishing of details required for Assessment and_ timely
declaration of Productivity Linked Bonus for the year 2012-13.
Sir,

Please refer to the above cited subject. The work relating to the assessment of
P.L. Bonus for the year 2012-13 has been taken up by the Headquarters. Ministry of
Labour & Employment vide their letter dated 15th March 2013 instructed EPFO to
review the new PLB Scheme as the ‘Productivity Factors’ might have changed and
directed to formulate a fresh PLB Scheme and send the same after getting it
recommended from the Executive Committee, EPF. Accordingly, a new PLB Scheme is
being formulated by the National Productivity Council (NPC). As it may take some time
in formulation and getting formal approval of the Central Government, hence it has
been decided to collect the information from all Regions relating to assessment of P.L.
Bonus with reference to existing the P.L.B. Scheme as approved by Government of
India in December, 1999. Information relating to parameters and performance as per
the Scheme is to be furnished, as usual, in the Annexure A to C (Forms enclosed).

ACCOUNTS & CASH

2. A time-limit of 30 days (calendar days) has been prescribed for completing the
job relating to settlement of PF, EPS and EDLI claims, Transfer cases and cases
pertaining to Advances. In case the job is not completed within 30 days, weightage
would be reduced to half for the work done beyond 30 days. Date of receipt of claim
form (complete in all respect) and the date of dispatch of cheque/transfer through
NEFT would be taken into account for reckoning 30 calendar days. In some of the
cases it was found that the date mentioned on the cheque is taken into account, which
is not correct. The actual dispatch of cheque takes much more time after the cheque is
prepared and signed by the authorized officer. In order to avoid delay in dispatch it
has been decided that only the actual date of dispatch of cheque as recorded on the
slip issued by the post office should only be taken into account. In other cases where
no cheque is to be issued like PPO, Transfer out not involving actual transfer of PF

accumulations etc., the actual date of issue of PPO and the date of actual transfer will
be taken into account.

3. As regards issue of “Annual Statement of Accounts”, it has been classified into
two groups, Viz. (1) current year’s Accounts slips issued and (2) Previous year’s
Accounts slips issued during the current year. Accounts slips relating to the “current
Year” and those pertaining to previous years but issued during the current year should
be shown separately. The Number of accounts slips issued with the help of outside
agencies and the number of accounts slips prepared and issued on computers of EPFO
may also please be furnished separately in Column 9 of Annexure “A”.

4. Activity “issue of cheque against the PPO of Monthly Pension cases” has been
added in the Bonus scheme, 1999. Those beneficiaries who opt to get Monthly Pension
through their Bank Accounts are sent cheques from the Regional/Sub-Regional Offices
itself. This activity has been included in the PLB Scheme, 1999 with a view to
encourage the staff members to issue the cheques of Monthly Pensions as promptly as
possible. Accordingly, information may be furnished separately for all the three
categories as provided in Annexure-A.

ENFORCEMENT & DAMAGES
5. The activities of “Enforcement & Damages” include:

(1) No. of 7A notices issued.

(2) No. of Speaking Orders of 7A passed and compliance effected.

(3) No. of Speaking Orders passed for Levy of Damages.

(4) No. of Recovery Certificates Executed:-
(a) For default in all the five Accounts (A/c No. 1,2,10,21 & 22)
(b) For default in 3 or 4 of the five Accounts.
(c) For default in 1 or 2 of the five Accounts.

7-A NOTICES

6. Only one notice has to be taken into account for all the three Schemes. In case
three separate notices are issued for the three Schemes, it has to be taken as one
only. Further, only the initial notice issued has to be taken into account and not the
notices issued every time after adjournment of proceedings due to any reason. With
the amendment of Section 7A, the RPFCs are required to decide not only the quantum
of dues but also to decide the Applicability. In such cases also if more than one notices
are issued, it should be taken as one only for the purpose of PLB return.

SPEAKING ORDERS OF 7A PASSED AND COMPLIANCE EFFECTED

7. Against this item all the speaking orders passed under Section 7A should not be
shown. Only those orders passed, which have been complied with, should be shown.
However, instructions contained in the preceding para as “7A Notices” should also be
kept in view.

Sir,
The reservation
policy in case of All India Recruitment
provides
for reservation
in the SC/ST /OBCs category
in the
ratio of 15/7.5/27
% respectively.
This ratio has to be maintained
on all India basis.
The information
collected
in response
to this office circular
no. HRM-IV/4(6)2010/6131
dated
13.06.2013,
it was found
that
majority
of the regions
were
maintaining
Reservation
Roster
on All India
Basis while
only a few of them
were
maintaining
Reservation
Roster
on State basis and the vacancies
arrived
on the basis
of different
reservation
roster
followed
by regions
were
notified
for SSA examination
2012 disturbing
a homogenous
platform.
This was perhaps
due
to different
interpretation
of Head Quarter
circular
No.SC-ST/9(1)06/JH
dated 05.04.2011.
Therefore,
the regions
adopting
State basis Reservation
Roster were advised
to prepare
reservation
roster
on All India
basis, so as to have uniformity
and maintain
same advantage/disadvantage
to all the categories.
It would
not be in the
spirit
of Reservation
Policy to adopt
one type of roster
for one place and another
type of roster
in other
place so as to
disturb
the overall
reservation
percentage
prescribed
to be maintained
at the
rate
15/7.5/27
% for SC/ST lOBe's
respectively
on All India Basis. Nevertheless,
this issue is being separately
referred
to DoPT for guidance/instruction.
The All India Roster
was also suggested
in view of the fact there
is no restriction
on reserved
category
to appear
as
reserved
candidate
across
India. In the recruitment
test and skill test held for post of SSA, reserved
categories
are being
given reservation
benefit
across
India. Further
in the examination
held for SSA for a particular
region, candidates
from
all over India are attracted
not necessarily
from a particular
locality or region as per the Hon'ble Supreme
Court order.
In such situation
it is advisable
to prepare
Reservation
Roster
on All India Basis for the time being which is subject
to
modification
as per clarification
from DoPT in this regard.
Any adjustment
in the vacancies,
if found not to be correct,
shall be carried
out in the next SSA examination.
However
disparity
on different
types
of reservation
roster
cannot
be
accepted.
You are
requested
to revise
the
reservation
roster
on All India
Basis & send
the
revised
vacancies
arising
as on
31.03.2012
within
two days positively.
You are also requested
to intimate
vacancy
position
of SSA as on 31.03.2013.

under section 7A but interest under section 7Q and damages under section

dues, as per section 11 of the EPF & MP Act, 1952.

TOUR OBSERVATION NOTE- PART-II
NUMBER OF ESTABLISHMENTSI
have observed during my visit
to various Regional Offices
that
the
number of establishments which are filing Electronic Challan cum Return (ECR)
are comparatively very less than the total number which have been issued the
provident fund number.
It
is understood that
more than 270;0establishments
are yet to be registered
on ECRportal. This excludes establishments which are
"pending for data release" and those in which "updation is not required".
In some cases, i.e. Chennai, the number of ECRcompliant establishments
is less than 750;0of the so called total
establishments.
It
has been further
observed that
most of establishments
who have not registered
on ECR portal
have closed down, some even legally. None of these units is paying even the
statutory
minimum charges.
All these non ECRfurnishing companies need to be classified with various
categories
(inoperative)
after
due verification.
This
should be done as a
campaign and by
01-11-2013 EPFO shall
have a clear
picture
of
all the
establishments.
This will also help in proper evaluation of the work load and
distribution
of same among the staff.
For example RO Chennai reports
that
there
are approximately
17,000 establishments
in total,
out of which about
3,300 establishments
are such in which "updation is not required"
and 110
establishments
are
"pending
for
release".
ECR filing
establishments
are
approximately
9100.
The workload/staff
demand is being raised taking the
number as 17,000, while it is well known that more than 4,500 establishments
have closed, even more than three years ago. Keeping such establishments alive
in EPF records is not good business practice.
There is an urgent need to gear up the Compliancemachinery. All the EPF
Regional and sub-Regional offices
shall, therefore,
carry an immediate exercise
to:-
1) Mark all non-functioning
establishments as closed/in-operative
after
due investigation, latest by 31st October 2013.
2) All
functioning
establishments
shall
be
ECR compliant,
i.e.
all
establishments registered on ECRportal shall be 1000;0ECRcompliant.
3) A special investigation shall be carried out to identify
and investigate
such establishments, which, even though are registered
on ECRportal
and shown as "complying", are in-fact remitting
only minimum statutory
dues.

Sub:-Disbursement of Pension through Core Banking Solutions
(CBS) of SBI, PNB and all other banks.

Ref:- CPFC’s e mail to ACC’s and RPFC’s on 23.08.2013.
Sir,
Please refer to the above said subject.

The Payment System in India has undergone a sea change in the
last few years and a number of initiatives have been undertaken to
meet the requirements of the public at large. CBS essentially helps in
integration of a range of services that are offered by banks including
direct payment in the account of the beneficiary on a real time basis. A
number of field offices of EPFO like Jabalpur,Dehradun and Amritsar
have taken advantage of CBS to disburse pension payment efficiently.
The same needs to be replicated on an all India basis to credit monthly
pension directly in the pensioners account on the last working day of
every month and, in exceptional cases, pension may be credited on
the first of the month. Such a step would go a long way in meeting
the legitimate expectations of pensioners who are entitled to timely
payment of pension. The adoption of CBS would substantially reduce
the grievances on account of delay in payment of pension.

The field Offices had been directed in the recent past to collect
core banking account number e.g. 11 and 16 digit savings bank
account number of SBI and PNB respectively. The core banking
account numbers which have since been collected by the respective
regional and sub- regional offices have extremely encouraging and

would be helpful in rolling out disbursement of pension on the CBS
platform. The system may be put in place for both the erstwhile
Family Pension Scheme, 1971 and the Employees’ Pension Scheme,
1995.

Every Regional and Sub-Regional! Office shall make available a
soft copy of the BRS (Bank Reconciliation Statement) to the link
branch to upload the data of the pensioner to directly credit the
pension on a real time basis in beneficiaries’ accounts in the paying
branches. The data of a pensioner may include name of the pensioner,
PPO number, savings bank account number and amount of pension.
Such an arrangement envisages intra-bank payment e.g. link branch
of SBI to paying branch of SBI and this would not involve any payment
settlement through NEFT since it does not involve inter-bank payment
e.g. from link branch of SBI to the paying branch of ICICI.

In future, the advance payment of pension may be remitted to
the bank one day before credit of pension on the last working day of
the month. All transfers to non-SBI banks may be effected through
RTGS/NEFT system of payment and such a transfer may also be
effected a day before the actual credit of pension. Any processing or
service charges incurred in electronic system of payment may be paid
from Account No. 10. The adoption of such an electronic mode of
transfer of money for disbursement of pension would cut down of float
money available with the bankers and EPFO can earn interest of up to
ten days with the new arrangement in place.

The undisbursed pension amount e.g. in cases of inactive
accounts in cases of death of pensioners, may be credited in the
pension disbursement account and the pensioners may be identified by
the link branch. A sample copy of the report of a particular link branch
is enclosed for information. The undisbursed amount may be credited
to Account No.10 through RTGS / NEFT in cases of inter-bank
settlement of payment e.g. link branch of PNB to Account No.10 in link
branch of SBI and the undisbursed amount may not be left idle with
the link branch. This system, thus, ensures that reconciliation is
immediate and, thereafter, service charge may be paid promptly to the
banks by the field offices.

All RPFCs are directed to ensure that pension payment for the
month of September, 2013 and thereafter every month is paid through
the CBS platform only. RPFCs may deploy personnel at any level as
per their requirement so that the target date for pension payment
through CBS is achieved without any postponement of the set date.

Scheme, 1995 (replacing Employees’ Family Pension
Scheme, 1971) and Employees’ Deposit-Linked
Insurance Scheme, 1976.

Sir
CPFC has visited some of the offices of EPFO recently to review the working
of EPF field offices.
Observations of CPFC, as contained
in his tour observation
report, are appended for your perusal and further
necessary action.
As would be evident from the contents of the said report, CPFC has flagged following issues for immediate
attention and for deploying necessary correctives:-
a)
Receipt & Dispatch Section is not being monitored properly. There must be a regular mechanism for
monitoring and handling of receipts. This should be priority area for Officers-in charge.
b)
Financial instruments (cheques/Demand
Drafts etc) must be properly accounted for and deposited in Bank
for realization in minimum possible time. Delays on this account entails loss of interest to EPFO.
c)
Negative balances need to be attended to on urgent basis.
d)
Pending bank reconciliation, both receipts and payments (including pension payments) side to be completed
on top priority. The pendency of bank reconciliation should not be more than two months at any point in
time.
e)
Accounts updation, duly contributing all members' accounts must be completed on top priority.
~
All pension disbursement accounts must be savings bank accounts only.
g)
The pension disbursement amount ought to be sent for disbursement at the fag end of the month and not
18th or 19th as is the practice today.
h)
CORE banking account numbers of all pensioners must be collected and updated in the system within two
to three months.
i)
All grievances must be entered in the EPFIGMS and attended to on top priority.
Yours sincerely

Sir,
The Government
of India,
Ministry of Finance, with
a view to provide
legislative synergy between the Income Tax Act, 1961
and the Employees'
Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act,1952 and to tackle the problems
faced by the small investors in the recognized provident funds, brought out an
amendment in Rule 4 of Part A of Fourth Schedule to Income Tax Act, 1961
by
Clause 56 of the
Finance Act, 2006
so as to provide that
recognition to a
Provident Fund under the Income Tax Act shall be restricted to only such funds -
a) which are covered under sub section (3) or sub section (4) of Section
1 of the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions
Act, 1952; and
b) which
have been exempted
under Section
17 of the
Employees
Provident
Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 from the
operation of any scheme framed therein.

Page 2 of 8




2.
Accordingly, in Rule 3, after sub rule (1) the following proviso was inserted
vide Finance Act, 2006, namely –

“Provided that in a case where recognition has been accorded to any provident
fund on or before the 31st day of March, 2006 and such provident fund does not
satisfy the conditions set out in clause (ea) of Rule 4, the recognition to such
fund shall be withdrawn, if such fund does not satisfy, on or before the [ 31stth
day of March, 2007], the conditions set out in the said clause and any other
condition which the Board may, by rules specify, in this behalf:

3.
Consequent upon such amendment, sub rule (1) to Rule 3 to Fourth
Schedule of Income Tax Act, 1961, now reads as :

“ The Chief Commissioner or Commissioner may accord recognition to any
provident fund which, in his opinion, satisfies the conditions prescribed in Rule 4
and the Rules made by the Board in this behalf, and may, at any time, withdraw
such recognition if, in his opinion, the provident fund contravenes any of those
conditions :
Provided that in a case where recognition has been accorded to any provident
fund on or before the 31st day of March, 2006 and such provident fund does not
satisfy the conditions set out in clause (ea) of Rule 4, the recognition to such
fund shall be withdrawn, if such fund does not satisfy, on or before the 31st day
of March, 2007, the conditions set out in the said clause and any other condition
which the Board may, by rules specify, in this behalf :”

4.
Further, in Rule 4, after clause (e), clause (ea) was inserted namely –

“(ea) the fund shall be a fund of an establishment to which the provisions of subsection (3) of Section 1 of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952 (19 of 1952) apply, and such establishment has been
exempted under Section 17 of the said Act from the operation of all or any of the
provisions of any Scheme referred to in that Section ;”

Agreement on Banking Arrangement between Central Board of
Trustees and State Bank of India- regarding.

The Agreement on Banking Arrangement of Funds belonging to and

under the control of Central Board of Trustees, Employees’ Provident Fund
Organization has been signed on the 8"" August 2013 with State Bank of India. The
said Agreement is effective from 1° December, 2012 and shall remain in force for
a period of three years.

2.

The salient features of the Agreement are as under:

Any delay in crediting the amounts over and above the time limit as
prescribed in para 5.5 of the Agreement or any delay in presenting the
Cheques/ Demand Drafts for clearing over and above the time limit as
prescribed in para 5.6 of the Agreement, shall attract payment of interest
for delayed credit, which shall be equivalent to 2% above the Savings
Bank interest rate of SBI as applicable from time to time and would be
credited in the respective account of the Trustees every month(Para 5.9).
The savings bank interest rate has been revised to 4% per annum w.e.f.
01.05.2011. Hence the interest on delayed credit is to be calculated
@6%(4%+2%) per annum.

Any dispute regarding the calculation of interest on delayed credits shall
be settled within one month by the officer-in-charge of the respective

field offices of the Trustees and concerned Link Branch of SBI.

Page 1 of 3

iil,

Vi.

Further, if any such dispute is not resolved within three months, the
Trustees shall be entitled to recover penal interest @ 4% p.a. over &
above the prevailing Savings Bank Interest rate of SBJ, on the amount
finally agreed as payable by SBI as "interest on belated credit" for the
period till its final settlement or actual! credit in the respective account of
Trustees.

There is no change in the ‘Service Charges payable to SBP on collection
of contribution t.e. the service charges would remain Rs.3.00 per Rs. 1000
on total monies received by Base Branches/Link Branches. However,
there shall not be any charge on other inter departmental
remittances/transfers as mentioned under para 5.17 of the Agreement.

Any dispute relating to charges, if any, debited by SBI should be resolved
by the nodal officers within three months from the date of such debits
failing which Trustees shall be entitled to penal interest of 4% above
prevailing Savings Bank interest rate of SBI on such excess charges
debited by SBI. SBI shall not be liable to pay the penal interest, if the
cause for the delay in settlement of dispute is attributable to
HO/RO/SRO/any other = official of the Trustees. Therefore,
RPFC(F&AVAPFC(Cash) of Regional/Sub-Regional offices shall be the
nodal officers for the purpose of resolving the issue of service charges.
They may take up this matter with concerned branch of SBI regularly to
ensure that the disputes are settled without any delay.

There should be a zero balance in the Account No. | & 10 of Field
Offices at the day end transferring the fund available (debit or credit
both) in A/c No. 1] & 10 to Central A/c No. 5 & 11 (Para 5.19.2.(3)

Interest on overdraft amount is charged by SBI, Mumbai Main Branch
centrally. Therefore, the link branches are not supposed to charge any
interest on overdraft amount in a/c no. | & 10 unless there is a situation
where debit balance available at link branch is not transferred/auto swept
to A/es No. 5 & 11 due to full utilization of OD limit at Mumbai Main
Branch. The cases of interest on overdraft charges by link branches, if
any, should be reported to Head Office invariably.

The overdraft limit is centrally maintained at SBI, Mumbai Main Branch
which is to be utilized by all RO/SROs as per their requirement.

Sub: Guidelines to be observed while sending supplementary budget proposals to
Head Office - reg.

Sir,
it is brought to your notice that allotment of budget is not an on-going activity. Fieid

Offices are supposed to incur only the expenditure duly sanctioned by the Competent
Authority, subject to availability of budget as per allotment of BE/RE by the Head Office.
2. However, it has been noticed that some of the offices habitually send requests for
additional allotment of budget immediately after receipt of BE/RE even if sufficient budget
is available to meet out their existing requirements.
(a) Many a time the request for grant of ex-post facto sanction / ratification / reappropriation/ additional allotment of budget under certain budget heads does not
contain any justification and details regarding actual expenditure incurred upto date that
are necessary for placing the proposal before the Competent Authority in Head Office or
invoive expenditure have been incurred without the sanction of the competent authority.
(b) In many cases, these requirements are not sent under the signature of RPFC-| of the
Region ignoring the budget available in other Sub Regional Offices.
3. As such before sending any request for additional allotment to Head Office, the
concerned Regional Office needs to ensure the following:-
i) References for ex-post facto sanction / ratification /re-appropriation/
additional allotment of budget should be self contained with full justification and
details regarding actual expenditure incurred upto date etc. and forwarded under
the signature of RPFC-I/Officer-in-Charge of the Region/NATRSS/EPFAT otherwise

Proposals will not be entertained at alll.

-2II) As regards budgetary matters, only Regional Offices should take up the
matter with Head Office. It is seen that some SROs/ ZTis refer such matters to Head
Office directly without getting the approval of the Officer-in-Charge of the
concerned RO/ NATRSS/ Head Office/ EPFAT. This practice should discontinue at
once. Such unauthorized references will not be entertained.

Il) In cases of non-recurring /Unusual expenditure such as on the opening of new
offices, visit of Parliamentary Committee etc., request for budget allotment should be
accompanied with a copy of the administrative approval of the Competent
Authority to incur the expenditure. The absence of such approval makes it difficult fo
process such proposals.

IV) The above instructions be followed consistently and with immediate effect.

{Issues with the approval of FA&CAO}.

Yours faithfully,

Subject: Consolidated guidelines for issuing Certificate Of Coverage (COC) — reg.

Sir,

Kind attention is invited to this office letter of even number dated 25/07/2013 whereby

it was conveyed that from 15" August, 2013 onward, the COCs will be issued by the

Regional/Sub Regionat office in whose jurisdiction the establishment in which the member is

employed is covered.

2. In this context it is mentioned that the process flow of the issuing COC was also

explained in Para 3 of the said letter. Nonetheless, with a view to have unambiguous clarity

and better understanding on the issue, the same is reiterated below in a consolidated

manner:
>

Vv

VW

All the applications for COCs will be received/acknowledged by the Inward
Section and entered into a separate register

All the applications received by the Inward Section will be forwarded directly
tothe RC (FA)/OIC as the case may be. Entry of these applications will be
made inaseparate register by the PA to RC(FA)/OIC and the applications
will be sent to the concerned Sections for verification of details of the
employee and signature of the employer or his authorized signatory

After verification the concerned Section will return the application to the PA
fo RC(FA)/OIC for being forwarded to the EDP Cell for data entry etc.

On receipt of an application in EDP, the data entry work will be done by the
concerned DEO/DPA

Verification of the data in the system through the application software would

be done by the Accounts Officer designated for this purpose

- ¥) cl } +5

> After verification/editing of the data, fair copies of the COCs will be printed
on good quality paper and put up for signature to RC(FA)/OIC, who are
authorized to sign the COCs

> Signed COCs will be dispatched through speed post without any delay to
the employer for being handed over to the employee concerned and
appropriate entries will be made in the register being maintained by PA to
RC(FA)

3. COCs in respect of non- EPF members e.g. employees of banks etc. are also
to be issued by EPFO. However, such COCs will be issued on receipt of an amount
of Rs. 10,000/- through bank draft payable to EPFO, which is to be deposited in A/c
No.2 (Admn Account) of the concerned RO/SRO.

4. As the details of issuing agency are to be mentioned in the COC, it is
necessary that the TELEPHONE/FAX number and the email address of the
concerned office/officer is indicated correctly. For this purpose, correct details in
respect of address, telephone number, email address etc. may be forwarded to
R.C (NDC) on his official mail id. Further, while issuing COC, it may be ensured that
each and every COC has the stamp of Logo of EPFO under the column relating
to “agency delivering the certificate” and it is signed along with the seal of the officer.

A scanned copy of the COC issued is enclosed for reference.

5. Besides, COCs can also be issued for the retrospective period if compliance
in respect of the member has been received by the office. It is also requested to

ensure that COCs are issued and delivered at the earliest.

6. Other technical guidelines on the issue are being issued by the RC(NDC)

separately.

Yours faithfully,

Sub : Workshop for Employers/EPF Members/Employers’ & Employees’ Representatives of
un-exempted establishments on 22nd & 23rd August, 2013 – regarding.

Sir,

We have the pleasure to inform you that Zonal Training Institute, East Zone, Kolkata is going to
conduct a Workshop for Employers/EPF Members/Employers & Employees’ Representatives of UnExempted establishments of Public/Private Sector on 22nd & 23rd August, 2013 at our aforementioned
address.


You will appreciate that highlighting of the benefits under EPFS-1952, EDLI-1976 & EPS-1995 to
the EPF Members/Employers/Employees’ Representatives including their duties and responsibilities assigned
as per the provisions laid down under EPF & MP Act 1952 and the Schemes framed thereunder are extremely
essential in the interest of EPF Organisation as well as of the subscribers. By this Workshop the level of
knowledge of the participants/subscribers will be enhanced and they will know the quantum of benefits
entitled under the schemes and also their rights and privileges admissible to them.

Although we have made some direct communications with the employers of the newly covered
establishments, we feel that an advice from your office will help more number of Employers to participate in
the Workshop. Hence this is to request you to intimate your member establishments for ensuring their
participation in this Workshop.


Each participant will be charged Rs.3000/- (Rupees three thousand only) as Course Fee for
providing working lunch, tea, snacks and course materials. One copy of Nomination Form is enclosed
[Please make photocopies if more required]. The fee is to be paid by cash or Demand Draft drawn in favour
of Zonal Training Institute, East Zone payable at Kolkata.


In view of the limited capacity at the venue, it will be highly appreciated if maximum of 03 (Three)
nominations from your member establishment are forwarded to this office latest by 19.08.2013 by Fax at
033-22258921.
Yours faithfully,
Enclo. : As above.

With an aim of providing quality services to all the stakeholders of EPFO, new
imtiatives and efforts are undertaken to deliver quick and hasste free services. In this
regard, many online facilities such as Know your EPF balance, Know your claim status,
EPFIGMS (Register your grievance) are made available for the EPF members through the
EPF website. Also, employers are given the facility of online submission of ElectronicChallan-Cum-Return (ECR). Online transfer claim settlement process will also be made
available very soon.

Hence, in order to bring to the notice of all concerned these new initiatives and
other ongoing activities of the organization, awareness programmes should be regularly
carried out by holding periodic meetings with the employers and employees.
interactions may be carried out on a regular basis by holding seminars / workshops /
educational camps etc. Employers’ association and workers unions must be associated
with the conduct of the same.

various functional parameters should be given adequate publicity by issuing press
statements by the ACC (Zones) and Regional P.F Commissioners-1 on a monthly basis.

information flow to the public. Such press releases may highlight the performance of
the office especially with regard to the number of settlements and volume of the
financial transactions, besides details regarding Bhavishyanidhi Adalats and punitive
actions taken against the defaulting establishments. Subsequently, press clippings may
be collected and archived for record and reference.

Subject: Image building through settlement of claims within 3 days — Regarding
Sir,

Please recall the meeting held on the above subject on 05-07-2013. The experience of some of
the offices which are doing outstanding work in the field of clatm settlement was shared and it was
decided that the settlement of claims shall be improved in all the offtces.

2. The performance of various offices was reviewed again on 26-07-2013. The data available on
the dash board shows some encouraging results. [t is thought pertinent to share the data among all of
us.

3. As on 03-07-2013, No. of claims pending for settlement beyond 30 days was 12,702, which is
now reduced to merely 5268.

4, As on 03-07-2013, there were 20 offices who were settling more than 60% claims within 3
days. As on 26-07-2013, there are 3 new offices which are settling more than 60% of the claims
within 3 days. The new offices to join this group are Mysore Road, Surat and Bharuch. The efforts
taken by these offices are noted with satisfaction.

5. In the meeting held 05-07-2013, it was also pointed that few of the offices have Very Good
productivity in terms of claim settlement. However, their effort does not get noticed because high
number of claims received which in turn precludes them from processing the claims within 3 days of
its receipt. The productivity to these offices needs to be recognized. For the figures of claim
settlement till 26-07-2013, the following 5 offices are best in terms of productivity of settlement of
claims per SSA.

7. The effort taken by all the officers and staff in the field is appreciable. CPFC has also
appreciated the commendable effort being made by all the officers and staff in reducing the time
period of settlement of claims from present 30 days to ultimately 10 days.

8. It is expected that you bring the appreciation of CPFC and the undersigned to the notice of

IMPORTANT
Subject: Implementing CCPAP Module.

Sir,

In order to improve accountability and bring-in utmost security in settlement of
claims through cheques, it was mutually decided by EPFO & SBI to implement CCPAP module
for payment of Provident Fund and Pension Fund amount to the beneficiaries. Under this
module, the details of the cheques issued by EPFO would be made available to SBI for
uploading the same on their server before the cheques are actually issued/presented for
clearance. Since the details of the cheques would be available with bank in advance, the
physical cheques presented for clearance will be matched by the bank with the details already
available on their server. Any change in the details made by the fraudster would be detected and
the cheques will not be honoured. Functionality for uploading the information relating to
cheques issued is separately being developed by IS Division and shall be intimated to you in
due course.

2. For payment through CCPAP (Corporate Cheque Payable at Par), the multicity
cheques type 29 is required. SBI has allowed CCPAP facility in the existing Current Account |
(EPF) and 10 (EPS). As a first step to operationalize CCPAP, all Field Offices were requested
to obtain multicity type 29 cheques for A/c No. 1 & 10 and CTS 2010 cheques for other
Accounts 2, 21 & 22. In this connection, the circular letters issued by Head Office on
01.03.2013, 15.03.2013 and 03.04.2013 (posted at SI. No. 625 and Sl. No. 656 of 2012-13 and
Sl. No 7 of 2013-14 under Office Order/Circulars on Official Website of the Organization) may
be referred.

3. Type 29 is the code of bank under which the CCPAP facility is available. This
code is mentioned on cheque leaves in the last where the cheque number and MICR number is
printed. A sample of type 29 cheque leave is enclosed for reference where the code 29 is
circled. It is noticed that some of the Field Offices have obtained simple multicity cheques
under code 11 on A/c No. | & 10 which is not in order. The specification of the cheque leaves
for different account is re-produced below:

e For Account No. 1 & 10 — Multi-city Type 29 cheques with CTS-2010
standard.
e For Account No.2, 21 & 22 —-CTS-2010 standard Multi-city cheques.

4, Despite the above referred circulars issued by Head Office, the Field Offices,
except a few, have not yet confirmed whether the required cheque leaves have been provided by
the bank and are in use. Therefore, FA & CAO has desired your intervention to ensure usage
of above type of cheques to prevent fraud and to submit information as per following

Sir,
Please refer to Head Office letter No. IS/Project I- Transfer claims/7846 dated

2. In the revised process to streamline the processing of transfer claims, it has been
decided that an option would be given to the members to submit the claims through online
mode. The online claim of transfer would be received from the member duly attested by
employer using digital signatures.
3. Thus for the online submission of claims, the registration of the digital signature of the
authorised signatories of the establishments is required for attestation of the claims. The
process to carry out the activity is explained under:

(a) The employer would fill up the details of the authorised signatories in the facility provided
to the employer at Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP) through EPFO website
www.epfindia.gov.in. The name, designation and mobile number of the authorised
signatories would be furnished by the employer. The employer can then upload the
digital certificates of the authorised signatories. The employer can upload the details of
maximum of three authorised signatories.

A letter (in duplicate) is required to be printed by the employer after uploading the digital
signatures of each of the authorised signatories. The print button given on the same web
page can be used for the purpose. The format of the letter is enclosed as Annexure A.
The letter is to be signed by the employer authorizing the officials of the establishment for
the purpose.

The letter printed for the purpose would also have to be signed by the authorised
signatories in the relevant column. This would help in the updation of specimen
signatures of authorised signatories with the field offices for processing of physical claims.
The letter (in duplicate) is to be submitted to the concerned field offices, where a task
would be pending in the RO/SRO Admin Portal (For OTCP).

A Nodal Officer, not below the rank of Accounts Officer, has to be deputed in each field
office for completion of registration process at EPFO end. The details of the Nodal Officer
deputed for the purpose i.e. Name of the Nodal Officer, Designation and his contact
number should be informed at e-mail ID webadmin-epfo@nic.in by 26/07/2013.

The Nodal Officer in each office would receive the letter from the establishment. The
nodal officer would make entry of the receipt of the letter at RO/SRO admin portal and
would send the letter (in duplicate) to the respective accounts group for verification.

The Dealing Assistant in accounts group would verify the signature of the employer from
the office record. He would keep one copy of letter received from the establishment for its
record and for specimen signature of authorized signatory. He would return the other
copy of the letter to the nodal officer after verification and approval by APFC of accounts
group.

On the receipt of above approval of APFC, accounts group, the nodal officer would
approve the pending task in the RO/SRO admin portal (For OTCP) for registration of
digital signature of the authorised signatory.

The employer can then digitally sign and submit the claims.

In case the employer wants to revoke the signature of the authorised signatory, he will
have the option to do so at Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP) through EPFO website.
On revocation, the digital signatures of the respective signatory would be suspended and
any digital claim received thereafter signed digitally by the respective signatory would be
rejected. A letter (in duplicate) is required to be printed by the employer after revoking
the digital signatures of the respective signatory, which would, then, be required to be

Subject:- Revised Transfer Claim Format — Handling of physical and digital claims
in the EPFO field offices.
Reference:-Head Office Letter No. Manual/ Amendment/2011/7368 dated

To

12.07.2013
Sir,
Please refer to Head Office letter dated 12.07.2013 on the subject cited above.
2. The need to streamline the processing of transfer claims has been felt for quite a long

time as a large number of grievances relate to transfer claims. The matter was discussed in
detail in the meeting with senior officers of EPFO on 01.04.2013 and 02.04.2013. Based on the
macro-level decisions taken in the meeting to modify the business processes, following broad
level process changes have been initiated -
a. The claims can be submitted through previous employer or present employer. The
additional option to submit the claim through the previous employer would expedite the
claim settlement process, as the information required from the previous employer would be
obtained along with the claim form.
The option to submit the claim through the present employer has been retained as at times
the member may find it difficult to obtain the signatures of the previous employer due to
change of location on change of job.
In order to provide this option of submission of the claims at transfer-out office as well as

transfer-in office, the Transfer Claim Form (Form-13) claim has been redesigned with three

parts:-

(i) Part A- Personal Information of member.
(ii) Part B- Details of Previous Account which is to be certified by the previous
employer. This would be optional with option C.
(It has been informed in the form that the settlement of claim would take
relatively less time in case the claim has been attested by previous employer.)
(iii) Part C- Details of Present Account which is to be certified by present employer.
This would not be required if part B has been certified by previous employer but it would
be mandatory in case Part B is not certified by previous employer.
b. An option would be given shortly to the members to submit the claims through online
mode. The member can fill up the form online on the Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP).
The member will have to take a printout of the claim, sign it and submit it to the employer.
The online transfer claim would be received in EPFO office after due attestation by employer
using digital signatures. In case of such online claims, the employer would not submit the
printout of the claim submitted by the member to EPF office. He would retain it with himself
for his own office record.
c. Since all the members may not have access to internet facility and all the employers
may not be able to file the digitally signed claims, the option to submit the claims through
physical form would also be allowed.
d. The online claim application can also be submitted through previous employer or
present employer. The online claim application, if submitted through previous employer,
would be settled in lesser time as the member's details with previous employer would be
provided in the form.
e. The online claims will be received by a central server which shall check the availability of
member details (i.e. Father’s/Husband’s name, relationship, Date of Birth, Date of Joining,
Date of Exit) in the database. In all such cases where the details are not available in the
database and the application has been received through present employer, the same is to be
obtained from the previous employer. A proper monitoring and tracking MIS about such
cases shall be maintained in the system for their expeditious disposal.
f. The physical claims received at the transfer-out office would be settled as is being
currently done on receipt of claim from transfer-in office. If the claim has been submitted at
the transfer-out office signed by the previous employer, the details verified by the previous
employer in Transfer Claim Form (Form-13) can be used to fill up the member’s missing

details.

Subject: Training Programme on “Enhancing Managerial Effectiveness”— Nomination(s) Regarding.

Sir,

The National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) is conducting a

three days Training Programme on “Enhancing Managerial Effectiveness” scheduled to be held from
21-23 August,2013in its premises at -

30-31 Institutional Area, D-Block, Janak Puri, New Delhi-110058.

The programme aims at equipping participants with self management techniques for
enhancing self effectiveness and thereby managerial effectiveness.

At the end of the course the participants would be able to:

e Enhance their self awareness with the aid of psychometric tools
e Apply inter-personal skills for self development.
e Enhance their leadership effectiveness applying various leadership theories.

You are requested to nominate two officers preferably of RPFC-II/ RPFC-I rank (failing

which APFC) from your region for this programme. It may also be ensured that no officer who is
retiring in this financial may be nominated.

The name of the nominated officer may please be communicated latest by 05.08.2013.
The accommodation in the hostel will be available from one day before the
commencement of the programme till one day after the completion of the training programme. Any

extension beyond this will require specific approval of Director, NATRSS.

You are requested to relieve the officer(s) with a direction to report to NATRSS on
21.08.2013 at 9.30 A.M. sharp.

(This issues with the approval of Director, NATRSS)
Yours faithfully.

OFFICE ORDER ‘70 JUL 2073

The Central Provident Fund Commissioner vide U.O. note no.ASD-|/Officer of
the Day/307 dated 09.07.13 {copy enclosed) has observed that the general
maintenance of the office in terms of cleanliness needs close monitoring and
improvement and the visitors to the office are not getting proper response. The
officers/officials leave their lights and other electrical appliances in switch on mode
and even internet systems are not switched off, causing loss to the organisation. He
desired that there is need to improve punctuality in the office for which bio nietric
attendance system has been started.

2. The key areas which need attention on everyday basis can be listed as follows:

i. Ensuring and monitoring of punctuality by officers and staff
ii. | Maintenance of general discipline in the office
iii. Attending visitors to the office and providing proper assistance to them
iv. Looking after cleanliness of the office, especially toilets
v. Monitoring the work and number of outsourced staff
vi. Arrangement of clean and safe water
vil. Monitoring the cleanliness and service of the canteen
viii. Ensuring proper functioning of all the gadgets such as intercom, airconditioned system etc.
ix. Ensuring that all gadgets are off when not in use, thus saving on energy
x. Monitoring the work of liftmen

3. Hence a close monitoring of above aspects bringing in perceptible
improvement in the working of the office is required which can be ensured by
posting /detailing an officer in rank of RPFC-| as ‘officer of the day’. This officer will
come to the office one hour before the office hours and check on all the points
mentioned in Para 2.

4. The functions listed in Para 2 are, however, suggestive. The “officer of the
day” is expected to be innovative and pro-active and check even other areas, say
roof top/ terrace of the building, cleanliness of overhead tanks etc. This officer will
generally be the /ast to /eave ensuring that the office is properly locked and energy
using devices are in on mode only if required to be used.

Contd...

visitors to the head office are properly attended to and their grievances are resolved.

of the field offices as well as the concerned sections in headquarters.

5. All divisional heads will provide full co-operation to the ‘officer of the day’.
This officer will also make a report in the evening in a register for the purpose to be

Sub: Outbound Training Programme on “Leadership & Team Building” scheduled to be held from
29" July -02" August, 2013 — Calling for Nomination(s) -regarding.

Sir,

The National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) is conducting a five
days Outbound Training Programme on Leadership & Team Building scheduled from 29™ July -
2" August, 2013 at Jaisalmer.

This outbound training programme aims af team building from the leadership perspective and to
underline the importance of individual in a tearm, The main objective of the course is to make the
individual aware of dynamics and constants of team building in varied work situations and to enable the
participants to achieve the common task.

The training will include adventure activities in addition to management exercises and classroom
sessions. Treks in the sand dunes, survival exercises etc. will be a part of the training. Only those
officers who are physically fit and capable of enduring extensive physical activity need apply for the
programme.

Nominations may please be sent to the undersigned by fax or e-mail, preferably before
12" July 2013. NATRSS will circulate the list of shortlisted participants on 15" July 2013, Detailed
itinerary of the programme alongwith instructions for participation will be communicated to shortlisted
officers individually through their controlling officers. The selected officers may be relieved accordingly.

The reporting and relieving point for the programme will be SRO Jodhpur. NATRSS will make
travel arrangements after report of duty at the reporting point. The officers will have to make their own
travel arrangements to & fro the reporting point. NATRSS will also coordinate board and lodge at the
training venue. The actual expenses towards the same will be borne by individual officers out of daily
allowance admissible under the rules.

The programme is designed to be especially beneficial for the officers performing leadership roles.
The officers in the cadre of ACCs/RPFC -I are, therefore, encouraged to participate in the programme.

(This issues with the approval of Director, NATRSS)

Sub: Modification in Para 16(5)(b) of EPS, 1995 under the EPF & MP Act, 1952.
Sir,

Certain instances have been referred to Headquarter where the nominee or dependent
father/mother of a deceased member, who had not rendered pensionable service on the date of

exit from the employment but had opted to retain the membership of the scheme, have claimed
Return of Capital under clause (b) of sub-para 5 of Paragraph 16 of EPS, 1995.

Although Para 13 has been deleted vide GSR 688 (E) dated 26-09-2008 but the provision
of Para 16(5)(b) referred to the deleted Paragraph 13 of EPS, 1995 and consequently no benefit
could be given creating an impasse.

Paragraph 16(5)(b) of EPS, 1995 has since been amended vide GSR No. 80(E) dated
14-02-2013 w.e.f. 26-09-2008 (EPF website Sr.No.641 of 2012-13) whereby nominee or
dependent father or dependent mother in such cases is entitled for withdrawal benefit as provided
in Para 14 of EPS, 1995.

You are requested to regulate the cases accordingly.

Sub: Image Building through Claim Settiement within 3 days.
Sir,

You are aware that in the Financial Year 2012-13, our Organisation has
settled 1.08 Crore claims, out of which 12.62 Lacs claimants were dissatisfied as
their claims were not settled within 30 days. Moreover, 1.41 Lacs claims were
not settled even after 90 days which has brought down the image of EPFO
amongst our members.

2. Genuinely, customers expect change in the mindset from 30 days fo
atleast 3 days in computerised era for withdrawing their own money.

3. Total 5,38,704 claims were pending as on 11.06.2013. For immediate
relief, Pendency Clearance Drive be launched immediately to settle 100%
claims received before 15th June 2013. This target should be achieved by |
July 2013 by adopting all possible measures.

4. After computerisation, 11.08 Lac (10.29%) Claims have been settled
within 3 days during financial year 2012-13. Whereas, for the period from
01.04.2013 to 11.06.2013 a total of 3,40,647 claims (15.66%) have been settled
within 3 days. Many outstanding offices have settled more than 60% claims
within 3 days and deserves applaud for achieving this greater efficiency. The
list of these image building ‘Star Offices’ is enclosed (Annexure ‘A’).

5. In 2013-14, 1.20 Crore claims are likely to be settled. For better image of
EPFO, claims needs to be settled within 3 days as being done in aforesaid 20
star offices. In all zones, claims settlement within 3 days is taking place as
evident from Annexure ‘B’. Average claim settlement within 3 days in these 20
star offices put together was 83.16% as on 11.06.2013. Out of the likely receipts
of 1.20 Crore even if lesser target of 70% claim settlement within 3 days is
considered at national level, it will benefit 84 lacs claimants. Hence, the target
fixing in this regard will uplift the image of EPFO. Accordingly, it has been
decided to hold a meeting on 5th July 2013 at 11.00 AM at Head Office for
finalising Action Plans for all offices for the year 2103-14.

Sir,

Several PA/PS have made representations for grant of arrears of pay & allowances
by conversion of notional benefit for the period from 14.7.1997 to 25.9.2000 into monetary
benefit in implementation of an Award dated 13.10.2004 passed by the Presiding Officer,
CGIT Cum Labour Court-II, New Delhi and upheld by Hon’ble Court, Delhi in WP No.WP(C}
40/2006.

The matter was referred to Internal Grievance Handling Committee. The
committee has opined that there was no disparity in the pay scale of Central Government
and EPFO. Therefore, monetary benefit cannot be given to PA/PS on account or arrear due
to order of CGIT and High Court as there was no discrimination of pay of Central
Government and EPFO.

Further, on the plea of applicants that few officials have been given arrears for the
period 14.7.1997 to 25.9.2000, the Committee has directed that the decision should be
revisited by respective Regional PF Commissioners.

It is, therefore, requested that a compliance report on above lines may be

forwarded to Head Office latest by 15.06.2013.

Accoqding to the Special provisions of the EPF Scheme 1952,
contributions in respect of an International Worker (i.e. employer's and employee's) were
required to be remitred by an employer on full pay (i.e. without ceiling of Rs.$5OOl per
month) w.e.f. 1" of November 2008 or from the date of joining, whichever was later. The
restrictions on the diversion of 8.33% From the employer's share of EPF contribution
towards the employvs' pension fund was also done away with vide GSR 149 dated
03/09/2010. Thus, it is very clear that in respect of the International workers, the
contributions had tabe deducted and remitted under EPF as well as EPS Scheme on full
pay without any ceiling (Where "Pay" wnsist of basic wages, Dearness allowance,
Retaining allowance (if any) and cash value of food concession (if any)).
In thisicontext while scrutinizing a case rcfu-red to the Head Office by the
Embassy of Republic of Peru, the following serious aberrations were noticed:
I. Even though @ International Worker had apparently joined service in a covered
establishment (WS Shipnet Software Solutions India Pvt Ltd.) on 1/4/2009, the
provident fun4 and pension contributions were deducted only from l'lune 2009.

2. The deduction of P.F. contribution as well as diversion of EPS contribution was
not being made on full Pby fiom due dates#
I
The instant case A ertains to Regional Ofice, Tambaram. However, other
field offices also might be having similar cases where employers arc not remitting the
contributions as per stipulated Law.
I
The cmploycrs need to be educated and updated appropriately about the
special provisions relating to the International Workers because such violations of the
provisions entail very serious consequences for the employers b y way of liability
towards both damages under section 14B and penal interest under section 74 including
prosecution under Section 14 of the EPF&MP Act1952. At the same h e , such
monitoring lapses on the part of @e EPFO field offices in ensuring proper administration
of the special provisions relating to the International Workers shall cause embarrassment
to the EPFO. However, more than anything else, an International Worker shall face
financial loss and great difficuhies when totalisation of benefits is attempted under
various Social Security Agreements.
The Regional PF Commissioners ,of the field offices arc expected to
streamline their enforcement machinery to ensure full compliance in respect of all
Internatid Workers. The data may be collected fiom FRROs fir cross checking to
ensure due compliance.
I
Willful defaulters m y also be considered for booking under Law to have
deterrent impact and ensuring stri~t compliance.
