Subject :- Provision for Revision and Rejection of erroneous ECR files-Reg.
Sir,

After the launch of ECR system from 01% April 2012, several offices had reported that

employers had submitted incorrect ECR files and are requesting for the correction of the same.

2. These problems could be broadly categorised as follows:-
(a) The Amount is swapped among different Accounts. For example, the amount of A/C 1
is swapped with the amount of A/C No. 10.
(b) The Amount/Details are swapped among different members.
(c) Remittance is made in some other establishment whether within the office or some
other offices.
(d) The wage month was incorrect.
3. IS division has recently provided the provisions for revising and rejecting such erroneous

ECR files. The user manuals for operating the provisions were provided along with the WAR

release.

4. Revision of Erroneous ECR files for the issues enumerated at 2(a) and 2(b) above, can be

done as under:-

(i) The revision of the details of the settled member is not permitted. For revising the
erroneous ECR files the employer will have to submit a request letter along with the
duly signed revised ECR generated through e-sewa portal. The total amount of the
revised ECR generated should match with the erroneous ECR and should include the

unaltered details of the settled members.

(ii) The Amount among the Accounts can be adjusted through Transfer Advice to the Bank

and the amount adjusted for establishment through previous year Adjustment function.

5. Rejection of Erroneous ECR files can be done for the issues enumerated at 2(c) and 2(d)

above. The following needs to be done:-

(i) The rejection of the ECR is not allowed if any settlement of claim is made in the
intervening period using the details of erroneous ECR.

(ii) Request is to be made by the employer. In case of 2(c) above the employer of the
establishment where the amount was erroneously paid will also have to agree that the
amount is to be paid to the correct establishment. .

(ii) The employer will submit the ECR through correct Employer e-sewa login, generate the
challan and submit the same in the EPFO office where the accounts of this
establishment are maintained.

(iv) The EPFO office where the amount was erroneously paid will do the following:-

(a)Total ECR amount will be reduced from Establishment ledger through the use of
Previous Year Adjustment Entry function.

(b) Erroneous credit to A/c No. 2, A/c No. 10, A/c No. 21 & A/c No.22 will be moved to
A/c Na.1 through the use of Misc. Payment with Dummy cheque. For crediting the
amount in A/c No.1 Misc. Receipt will be used.

(c) To move the payment to the concerned office, Misc. Payment with cheque will be
used.

(d) Cheque will be generated in favour of RPFC of the EPFO office where the

establishment A/cs are maintained.

(v) The EPFO office will then deposit the cheque in bank against the challan generated and
deposited by the employer.

6. It_is requested that _necessa actions ma lease be taken to correct the
erroneous ECR files by 31.05.2013

Sir,

Apropos the subject cited above, it would be appreciated that maintaining a
Strict security protocol is a sine qua non for the safety of any IT system. Several
instances have come to the fore where the users in various offices have failed to
adhere to basic security protocols and have ended up sharing their user IDs and
passwords with others thereby seriously endangering not only their own professional
careers but also compromising the financial integrity of the Organisation. Serious
frauds have been detected. Accordingly following measures are suggested for sincere
adherence:

1. Server Room should be secluded and must be under Lock and Key.

2. Entry to the server room must be restricted, and Complaint Registers, Log

Register may be maintained as prescribed.

The backup procedures must be followed strictly (Daily, Weekly and Monthly)

4. The daily backup must be kept in safe custody and a copy of the backup has to
be sent to other office as suggested in the Officer Order’ RI/PRM/2009/Vol.11/558/49123 dated 10.11.2010.

5. Password must be changed periodically, and should be sufficiently resistant to
cracking.

6. Password must be a combination of Upper Case, Lower Case, Special Character
and numeric digit.

7. Before truncating nicepfo_audit table, necessary permanent backup has to be
taken without fail and the backup files have to be maintained properly with
proper register entry.

8. No user should be allowed to access the internet while working in the
application software or connected to the LAN.

9. The PC connected in the MPLS cloud should not be exposed to the Internet.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject: Grant of Dearness Relief to Central Government
pensioners/family pensioners — Revised rate effective
from 1.1.2013.

The undersigned is directed to refer to this Department’s
OM No. 42/13/2012-P&PW(G) dated 4° October, 2012 on the subject
mentioned above and to state that the President is pleased to decide
that the Dearness Relief (DR) payable to Central Government
pensioners/family pensioners shall be enhanced from the existing rate
of 72% to 80% w.e.f. 1°" January, 2013.

2 These orders apply to (i) All Civilian Central Government
Pensioners/Family Pensioners (ii) The Armed Forces Pensioners, Civilian
Pensioners paid out of the Defence Service Estimates, (ili) All India
Service Pensioners (iv) Railway Pensioners and (v) The Burma Civilian
pensioners/family pensioners and pensioners/families of displaced
Government pensioners from Pakistan, who are Indian Nationals but
receiving pension on behalf of Government of Pakistan and are in receipt
of ad-hoc ex-gratia allowance of Rs. 3500/- p.m. in terms of this
Department’s OM No. 23/1/97-P&PW(B) dated 23.2.1998 read with this
Department’s OM No, 23/3/2008-P&PW(B) dated 15.9.2008.

3. Central Government Employees who had drawn lumpsum
amount on absorption in a PSU/Autonomous body and have become
eligible to restoration of 1/3 commuted portion of pension as well as
revision of the restored amount in terms of this Department's OM No.
4/59/97-P&PW (D) dated 14.07.1998 will also be entitled to the payment
of DR @ 80% w.e.f. 1.1.2013 on full pension i.e. the revised pension
which the absorbed employee would have received on the date of
restoration had he not drawn lumpsum payment on absorption and
Dearness Pension subject to fulfillment of the conditions laid down in para
5 of the O.M. dated 14.07.98. In this connection, instructions contained
in this Department’s OM No.4/29/99-P&PW (D) dated. 12.7.2000 refer.

4. Payment of DR involving a fraction of a rupee shal! be
rounded off to the next higher rupee.

Sub: Acquiring of requisite qualification by the left out DEOs for conversion to the
post of DPA - Regarding

Please refer to the subject captioned above.

Consequent upon the restructuring of the cadres of Information Service (IS) Division,
the conversion of DEO’s into the cadre of DPA have been made in accordance with the
notified Recruitment Rules of the said post. The RRs for the post of DPA provides that as a
one time relaxation, the existing regular DEOs (Gr. ‘A’)/(Gr. ‘B’)/(Gr. ‘C’) who do not possess
the minimum educational qualification will be appointed on regular basis on acquiring the
minimum educational qualification within two years from the date of notification of the
Recruitment Rules on 30.5.2009.

However, there are some cases where the DEOs could not acquire the requisite
qualification for DPA within the specified period of two years i.e. by 30.5.2011 but acquired the
qualification subsequent to this date. It has been decided to examine all such cases of left out
DEOs for conversion to the post of DPA.

In this connection, it is requested to furnish details of left out DEOs who acquired the
requisite qualification as per the Recruitment Rules of DPA after the stipulated period i.e.
30.5.2011 onwards to till date. A copy of the Recruitment Rules for the post of DPA is
attached.

Sub:
Action taken on the recommendations of Parliament Committee
on
Petition on pending court cases of EPFO- reg.
Sir,
Please find enclosed a copy of the recommendations of the Committee on
Petitions made in their 14threport (15th Lok Sabha). While acknowledging the efforts made
by the organization in handling the court cases,
the
Petition Committee has further
recommended for:
1. A
foolproof system to
be worked out to keep track of performance of the panel
advocates.
2. To ensure filing of prosecution casesagainst the defaulters.
3. To get maximum number of stay cases vacated and recover the locked up NRI dues
for crediting the same to members account.
4.
Result oriented policies to be formulated and put in place to counter the practice of
taking stay orders
by the defaulting companies. This should be followed by routine
supervision
to ensure that
policies are
strictly complied with by the concerned
authorities.
5. The panel counsels should be advised to file advance caveats in the courts to check
the tendency of defaulting companies from getting stay orders.
6.
In the states like West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka , Kerala , Madhya
Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat,
Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, where the
conviction rate is dismal, the Committee recommended to implement result oriented
action plan and implement and supervise the same to contain default.
7. The Committee viewed that merely issuing specific instruction to low performing
regions without
supervision or follow
up action will
not yield desired results.
Therefore, regular supervision monitoring and assessment of each office is essential.
8. Initiatives
to be taken up for setting up for special courts /special benches for
hearing EPFOcases.
Therefore, in the light of the recommendation of the Parliament Committee on
Petitions,
corrective
actions
as mentioned above
are required to be taken. Also if any
further
action as required due to the specific need of the region, it should be evaluated and
taken up immediately.
You are requested to devise the action plan to deal with the issue
under intimation to Head Office.

Subject: Amendment of Para 62 of EPF Scheme 1952 on ‘Financing of Members’ LIC

Sir,

policies’ — Inviting suggestions from the field offices — Regarding.

May kindly refer to the subject cited above. A proposal has been received in Finance

Division suggestions therein to delete the para 62 of the EPF Scheme 1952 on ‘Financing of
Members’ LIC Policies’. It was suggested in the said proposal that often LIC policies get lapsed
after one or two years normally due to the following reasons:

i)

ii)

lil)

iv)

v)

Policy document is maintained and premium is paid by EPFO. Member (s) often forget
the fact that there is LIC in their name and whenever they changes his job/estt, they do
not intimate concerned PF office resulting in lapse of the policy as next premium is not
paid.

Most of the members get their PF settled on change of job

After availing advances on various grounds, members do not have sufficient balance in
their account to pay the next premium and LIC policies get lapsed and member lost his
hard earned money to the LIC

In many cases, when members face un-expected/emergency situations and need
advances from their PF account, balance in their account is not sufficient since
substantial amount has been drawn towards LIC premium.

Since LIC policies are financed from member’s PF account, due to non-availability of
sufficient balance, it deprives the member from full benefits to the extent of EDLI
Scheme 1976, in case of unfortunate death.

Further, complaints have also been received wherein LIC agents often make allegations of
corruption against EPFO for not processing the LIC applications.

As para 62 is an important provision of EPF Scheme 1952, comments/suggestions of all the
field offices are solicited for further deliberations before taking any decision on
withdrawing/deletion of Para 62 of the EPF Scheme by the competent authority.

All suggestions/comments on the issue can be sent within 10 days through fax on
(011-26194349) or emailed at www.rc.fa@epfindia.gov.in

vide Office Memorandum No. 7(1) E.Coord/2012 dated 05.06.2012 on Expenditure
Management - Economy Measures and Rationalization of Expenditure of Ministry of Finance,
Department of Expenditure, conveyed by this office letter cited above, for a mandatory cut
in Non plan Expenditure on administrative expenses, austerity measures have been
implemented under certain budget heads in Contingencies & Misc. Section while allocating
the Budget Estimates for 2013-14. All Regional Offices/ Field Offices are requested to
manage their expenditure accordingly.

2/3

q)

b)

Provisions of Chapter 5 of General Financial Rules, 2005 and the principles of
financial propriety provided therein should be followed in letter and sprit before
sanctioning expenditure.

The expenditure should be properly identified and if must be charged to the
relevant budget head only.

Expenditure should be incurred after due sanction by the Competent Authority
and subject to the availability of budget as allotted in the Budget Estimates.

No commitment of expenditure should be made without asceriaining the
availability of funds in the budget.

No Expenditure should be incurred over and above the funds allotted under
each budget head.

Expenditure should be need based and not on the basis of funds available.
No request for ratification of excess expenditure would be considered.

The Budget Control Register must be maintained properly and kept up-to-date
so that any excess expenditure over allotment is noticed immediately.
RPFC-IIF&A) and RPFC-I, in-charge of the Region must regularly check the
Budget Control Register.

“Computerization”, “Staff Welfare Fund”, "Purchase of Motor Vehicles” "Office
Equipments(Air-Conditioners), “Fixture & Furniture’(Modular Furniture) and
“Capital Expenditure” may be forwarded directly to respective Divisional
Heads in Head Office.

In exceptional cases reference should be made to Head Office for allotment of
additional budget with full justification detailing the need.

RPFC of the Region shall personally ensure that there is no violation of
General Financial Rules and Principles of Financial Propriety in their
Region/SROs/Other Offices.
